papers.title: APED-CXR: Adaptive Privileged Evidence Distillation for Chest X-Ray Grounding with Image-Only Inference
papers.abstract: Compact chest X-ray (CXR) models that localize findings suit deployment, but box annotations are limited and report-aware multimodal models are expensive at inference. We introduce APED-CXR, which distills report-informed spatial evidence from a frozen multimodal teacher into a student with 11.1M parameters that predicts diseases and boxes from shared evidence maps and requires the image alone at test time. During training, the teacher uses the radiograph, report, and queried class to evaluate regions proposed from the student's current evidence maps, and its support scores serve as training targets for the student's pooled evidence scores within these regions. Trained on PadChest and evaluated on held-out PadChest-GR, refreshing the student's proposals for teacher evaluation improves box-level localization F1 from 0.302 with fixed warm-up proposals to 0.338 (IoU >= 0.5; gain 0.036, 95% CI [0.022, 0.049]), while maintaining diagnostic AUC. This gain depends on the teacher checking current proposals: with equally many random boxes, a fixed dense box set, teacher-generated boxes, or report rules instead of the teacher, F1 stays near the fixed-proposal level, and proposals two refreshes old recover only part of the gain. On NIH ChestX-ray14, a secondary test set, box recall also rises from 0.423 to 0.447.

papers.title: Direct Injection of Chemically-Enhanced Plasma into a Solar Flare Arcade
papers.abstract: The magnetic reconnection event that drives "standard" solar flares ejects material from the reconnection site, loading mass directly onto the newly-reconnected flare arcade. To et al (2024) suggested that this model can explain observations of the distribution of elemental abundances measured in post-flare loops: the reconnection exhaust directly injects plasma with coronal abundances onto the arcade, flowing from the apex downwards. We test this idea directly by modeling the spatiotemporal variation of elements with low first ionization potential (FIP), and directly inject material near loop apices. We show that this direct injection is capable of producing enhancements similar in magnitude and spatial spread across the corona to those observed during the gradual phase of an X11.9 flare. We also show that direct chromospheric heating strongly limits the width of the low-FIP enhancement to a narrow region near the injection site. The enhancement of low-FIP elemental abundances naturally explains bright knots commonly observed near the top of flare arcades.

authors.name: Andy S. H. To
authors.institution: European Space Research and Technology Centre

papers.title: Back Up Before You Regret: Measuring Backup Awareness and Automating Backup in Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents now complete tasks autonomously, modifying real-world state such as artifacts, software environments, and configurations along the way. Yet they show limited backup awareness: recognizing that an action will modify state that may later be needed, and preserving it beforehand. To evaluate backup awareness, we introduce RegretBench, a benchmark of 205 executable tasks grounded in regret moments reported on platforms such as X.com, GitHub, and Stack Overflow, where users explicitly regretted not preserving state they later needed. Across six frontier models, agents complete 86.1% of tasks on average yet back up before these moments in only 15.2%, showing that task completion ability does not imply backup awareness. Because it is hard to predict which changes will be regretted, we propose BackUpper, a harness plug-in backup layer that checks every tool call and preserves affected state before modification. It combines rule-based strategies for common operations with a lightweight subagent for complex cases, and its rule table can expand with subagent decisions over time. On RegretBench, BackUpper covers every regret moment action and restores states with 92.2% average similarity to the original. Achieving this costs only $0.014 per task, with 7x fewer tokens than the main-agent self-backup baseline. When users have preferences on what to back up, BackUpper can also narrow its scope accordingly, matching human annotations on whether an action is worth preserving with an 84.5% F1 score. These results suggest that agents can keep actions reversible at low cost while respecting users' preferences.

authors.name: Simon Yu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: RubricOpt: Self-Revision of Semantic Rubrics for Preference Optimization
papers.abstract: A model's failures can reveal gaps in the behavioral criteria guiding its training. We introduce RubricOpt, a framework that lets a policy revise these criteria within preference optimization. The policy diagnoses its own rubric-free outputs, retains requirements already covered by the rubric, and edits clauses that leave recurring failures unaddressed. A shared semantic representation connects task demands, preference-data contrasts, and rubric clauses, while a deterministic gate checks evidence references and fixed semantic anchors. The rubric then guides Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) during training, with preference pairs, labels, and the objective held fixed, and is removed at evaluation. Our analysis relates the local effect on rubric-free success to semantic alignment and a residual beyond the measured factors. Experiments on capability and open-ended generation benchmarks show that rubric conditioning can improve outcomes over ordinary DPO, with gains and regressions varying across models and datasets. A matched continuation isolates the contribution of revision from additional training and finds mixed incremental effects for the tested edit, whose feedback overlaps the evaluation set. RubricOpt thus brings the behavioral specification itself into the policy's feedback loop.

authors.name: Wei Chen
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Zhiheng Zhou
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Private Online Prediction from Experts with Small Losses
papers.abstract: We consider online prediction from experts, a fundamental problem in machine learning, under differential privacy constraints. Existing private algorithms achieve near-optimal regret $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T})$, where $T$ is the time horizon. However, this bound becomes suboptimal when $L^\star$, the cumulative loss of the best expert, is significantly less than $T$. In this work, we present the first differentially private algorithm with regret $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{L^\star})$, offering a substantial improvement in the low-loss regime. Our regret bound matches the non-private lower bound up to poly-logarithmic factors for constant privacy parameters, demonstrating that privacy incurs only a small cost in this setting. Our result assumes that the input sequence is oblivious, i.e., it is fixed in advance and independent of the algorithm's outputs. We also prove that an $\tildeΩ(\sqrt{T})$ regret is inevitable for adaptively generated inputs, even when $L^\star = 0$.

authors.name: Peng Ye
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Prefix Visibility Ratio: Quantifying Partial Observability in Carpet Bombing Detection
papers.abstract: Carpet bombing attacks distribute malicious traffic across many destinations within a network prefix, while operational monitoring commonly provides destination-specific telemetry for only a subset of those targets. This creates an attack-conditional observability problem that is not captured by address utilization or nominal monitoring coverage. We introduce the Prefix Visibility Ratio (PVR), defined as the fraction of attacked destinations for which the telemetry required by the host-level evidence plane is available, and argue that PVR should be treated as an explicit evaluation dimension for carpet bombing detection. We then present VANTA (Visibility-Aware Network Threat Analysis) as one concrete way to operationalize this principle. VANTA combines host-level and prefix-level anomaly scores, estimates PVR online from router-side destination evidence and the monitored-destination inventory, and adjusts evidence fusion according to both estimated visibility and estimator confidence. Across a validated campaign of 2,160 Mininet runs, VANTA achieves 99.18% precision, 93.46% recall, a global F1-score of 96.24%, and a 1.54% false-positive rate. In a separate matched-observability study using task-adapted feature-level reference implementations, VANTA reaches 95.89% pooled F1 and 92.39% recall for configured PVR<=10%, with its largest advantage appearing at configured PVR=1%. These reference comparisons are intended to isolate observability effects under a common binary detection task rather than to reproduce the original end-to-end objectives of the referenced systems. The results establish attacked-destination visibility as a measurable factor that can materially change detector behavior and should be reported explicitly in future carpet bombing evaluations.

authors.name: Eve Lin
authors.institution: Atma Jaya Catholic University of Indonesia

papers.title: Gibbs and Einstein in 1902: Parallel Constructions in Statistical Mechanics
papers.abstract: This article reexamines the striking conceptual and formal parallels between Josiah Willard Gibbs Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics and Albert Einstein first paper on statistical mechanics. Although their derivations follow different paths, both arrive at the canonical distribution and construct closely related theoretical frameworks for thermal equilibrium. Each offers a mechanical grounding of the second law of thermodynamics and defines temperature as the quantity that equalises when systems exchange energy, thereby characterising equilibrium without recourse to kinetic theory. In both cases, the constructions rely on general mechanical principles, most notably energy conservation and Liouville theorem, combined with probabilistic reasoning, and deliberately set aside Boltzmann kinetic approach. Whereas Gibbs treatise quickly became a canonical reference, Einstein 1902 paper remained marginal in both physics and its historiography for more than half a century. Focusing primarily on that first article, while also considering the closely related papers of 1903 and 1904, the present study reviews the main historiographical interpretations of their reception. Particular attention is given to Paul Hertz two critical articles of 1910, which identified a close affinity between Gibbs's and Einstein's approaches and played an important role in Einstein subsequent distancing from his early statistical programme, following a private meeting in Basel that Einstein sought in preference to a public controversy. Drawing on new archival evidence concerning the rapid European dissemination of Gibbs book in the spring of 1902, the article reassesses the plausibility of Einstein later claim that he was unaware of Gibbs work at the time.

authors.name: Hector Giacomini
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Short sums of the Möbius function over function fields
papers.abstract: We develop a new method which allows us to estimate, with a power saving, sums of the M{ö}bius function over function fields ${\mathbb F}_p(X)$. The sums run over monic polynomials with all other coefficients in short intervals, of length below the Pólya--Vinogradov threshold $p^{1/2}$. A classical result of L. Stickelberger (1898) reduces this question to bounding character sums with polynomial discriminants which are inhomogeneous multivariate polynomials. Variants of Burgess's method with non-linear shifts {\it {à} la carte} are introduced to go beyond the Pólya--Vinogradov range, combined with a stratification result of J. Xu (2020) for complete character sums.

authors.name: Etienne Fouvry
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Strong gradient absorption and initial decay prevent blow-up
papers.abstract: Consider positive classical solutions of the Cauchy problem for $u_t-Δu=u^p-μ|\nabla u|^q$, with sufficiently smooth initial data $u_0$, in the strong absorption regime, namely $q\ge p>1$ and $μ>0$. It has remained a long standing open problem whether finite time blow-up can occur if $u_0$ decays at space infinity. We here solve this problem, showing that the answer in negative. To this end, we establish a novel, universal Bernstein-type gradient estimate, of independent interest, valid only in the range $q\ge p$. Moreover, the decay assumption on $u_0$ turns out to be essentially optimal. Indeed we show that the solution blows up in finite time whenever $u_0$ has a positive limit at infinity, and we determine the blow-up behavior of $u$ at space infinity under an additional assumption.

authors.name: Philippe Souplet
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: On Euler's abelian relation of the web induced by the forgetful maps on the moduli space $\boldsymbol{\mathcal M_{0,n+3}}$: the case when $n$ is even
papers.abstract: In a previous paper ${\bf [P1]}$, for every $n\geq 2$, we studied the curvilinear web $\boldsymbol{\mathcal W}_{0,n+3}$ on the moduli space $\boldsymbol{\mathcal M}_{0,n+3}$, defined by the $n+3$ forgetful maps $ \boldsymbol{\mathcal M}_{0,n+3}\rightarrow \boldsymbol{\mathcal M}_{0,n+2}$, with particular emphasis on its abelian relations. In particular, when $n$ is even, we conjectured an explicit formula for its Euler abelian relation. This relation is constructed à la Gelfand-MacPherson from an invariant differential form representing the appropriate power of the Euler class of the tautological bundle of the Grassmannian manifold $G_2^{\mathrm{or}}(\mathbf R^{n+3})$ of oriented $2$-planes in $\mathbf R^{n+3}$. In this note, we obtain an explicit antisymmetrized formula for Euler's abelian relation for every even $n\geq 2$, and prove that it coincides, up to the explicit factor $-(n+1)(n+2)/2$, with the formula conjectured in ${\bf [P1]}$, which is therefore established for all even $n$.

authors.name: Luc Pirio
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Asymptotics of Masur-Veech volume of strata of quadratic differentials with many simple poles
papers.abstract: We provide large $n$ asymptotics of the Masur-Veech volumes for strata of quadratic differentials of the form $\mathcal{Q}_g(n,d_1,\dots,d_k,-1^{n+D-4g+4})$, where all positive integers $d_i$ are fixed and $D=d_1+\dots+d_k$. Our formulae are particularly explicit in genus $1$. For the two series of non-varying strata $\mathcal{Q}_1(n,-1^n)$ and $\mathcal{Q}_1(n,1,-1^{n+1})$ we give simple closed formulae for the volumes for any $n$.

authors.name: Anton Zorich
authors.institution: Institut de Mathématiques de Jussieu-Paris Rive Gauche

papers.title: Exotic vortex states and enhancement of orbital upper critical fields in an $s$-wave quasicrystalline superconductor
papers.abstract: Quasicrystals possess long-range order without translational symmetry, giving rise to intrinsically inhomogeneous superconducting states. Using the Bogoliubov-de Gennes mean-field theory, we investigate vortex states in an $s$-wave quasicrystalline superconductor on the Ammann-Beenker tiling, with particular emphasis on the high-field regime. We find that the vortex configuration can differ qualitatively from the Abrikosov triangular lattice. In particular, at filling $ν=0.8$, vortices preferentially penetrate weak-pairing regions centered on sites with coordination number $8$, indicating that their spatial organization is strongly influenced by the local geometry. Furthermore, we observe an enhanced upper critical field. At $ν=0.8$, where the enhancement is particularly pronounced, the spatially averaged order parameter exhibits a plateau-like field dependence accompanied by the formation of vortex clusters. These clusters accommodate additional flux in locally weak superconducting regions, providing a microscopic interpretation of the plateau-like behavior. Moreover, the upper critical field increases upon cooling toward zero temperature without a clear sign of saturation.

authors.name: Takumi Fukushima
authors.institution: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science

authors.name: Anuradha Jagannathan
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: A hybridization-derived interior penalty Nitsche method for heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion
papers.abstract: We develop an interior penalty Nitsche finite element formulation for heterogeneous and anisotropic diffusion problems, which is derived from an interior-penalty stabilized Lagrange multiplier method. A distinctive feature of the derived method is that it simultaneously combines two popular stabilization strategies: (i) a boundary penalty mechanism similar to Nitsche's methods and (ii) an interior penalty mechanism as for Continuous Interior Penalty (CIP) methods. Furthermore, the normal component of the numerical flux is single-valued across the mesh skeleton and available in closed form. We establish the equivalence between the hybridized Lagrange multiplier formulation and its condensed Interior Penalty Nitsche (IPN) form, and we deliver the stability and convergence analysis of the latter. For sufficiently regular solutions, we establish energy-norm error estimates for the three symmetry variants. Under a piecewise elliptic regularity assumption on the adjoint problem, the $L^2$ estimate is optimal for the symmetric variant and exhibits a half-order loss for the incomplete and nonsymmetric variants; its constant may depend on the diffusion coefficients through the adjoint regularity constant. This single-valued numerical normal flux, available in closed form, provides a starting point for locally conservative $H(\mathrm{div})$-conforming flux reconstruction, left for future work. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Upper and lower bounds for heat kernels with very strong degeneracy
papers.abstract: We consider the following degenerate parabolic equation on a bounded domain of $\mathbb{R}^d$ containing $0$: $\partial_t u - \nabla\cdot(\varphi(t, x) \nabla u)= 0$, where $\varphi$ is a rough weight behaving like $|x|^θ$ near $0$ for some $θ\geq 2$, and $u$ satisfies Neumann boundary condition. We prove that this equation admits a heat kernel with upper and lower Gaussian-type bounds.

authors.name: Hector Bouton
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Ideal class groups of certain real quadratic number fields and factorizations of values of certain quadratic polynomials
papers.abstract: We determine the odd primes $p$ for which the number of distinct prime divisors of $d-x^2$ is at most $2$ for every positive odd integers $x\leq\sqrt{p}$. We also determine the odd primes $p$ for which the number of distinct prime divisors of $2p-x^2$ is at most $2$ for every positive even integers $x\leq\sqrt{2p}$. To this end, we show that these properties of $p$ and $2p$ impose restrictions on the class numbers and fundamental units of the real quadratic fields ${\mathbb Q}(\sqrt{p})$ and ${\mathbb Q}(\sqrt{2p})$.

authors.name: Stéphane R. Louboutin
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Using Temporal Replication and Partial Pooling to Improve Practical Identifiability in Presence-Only Poisson Point Process Models
papers.abstract: Species distribution models based on thinned point processes are now commonly used in ecology to analyze presence-only data collected through citizen science, including in spatio-temporal frameworks. A key challenge in these models is the separation of the ecological process from the observation process, which raises identifiability issues. Here, we investigate the theoretical and practical identifiability of a thinned Poisson point process model. We show that, with a log link for ecological intensity and a logit link for observation probability, the model can be structurally identifiable under simple conditions, provided that observation probability varies spatially. We then evaluate the benefits of using temporal replication within a spatio-temporal framework to improve estimation when ecological intensity and observation probability are weakly separated. We quantify these benefits through simulations. The results highlight persistent practical identifiability problems affecting the ecological and observation intercepts, especially when observation probabilities are low. However, in a spatio-temporal model with partial pooling, these parameters are estimated more accurately than in a single-year model, even when only a short time period is considered. Temporal replication also improves estimation of parameters shared across years. Finally, we illustrate the use of such a spatio-temporal model through a study of coypu (Myocastor coypus) distribution in Occitanie, France. Overall, our results show that temporal replication can partially alleviate practical identifiability problems in presence-only point process models when independent data sources are unavailable.

authors.name: Iris Lang
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Olivier Gimenez
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Revisiting the infinite Galois correspondence via group representations
papers.abstract: Inspired by Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem, we interpret the Galois correspondence as a special case of a simple general principle in harmonic analysis on profinite groups. This also gives a representation-theoretic characterisation of profinite groups.

papers.title: Extending AMIRAL's blind deconvolution of Adaptive Optics corrected images with Markov chain Monte Carlo methods
papers.abstract: Adaptive optics (AO) corrected image restoration is particularly difficult, as it suffers from the lack of knowledge on the point spread function (PSF) in addition to usual difficulties. An efficient approach is to marginalize the object out of the problem and to estimate the PSF and (object and noise) hyperparameters only, before deconvolving the object using these estimates. Recent works have applied this marginal blind deconvolution method, combined to a parametric model of the PSF, to a series of AO corrected astronomical and satellite images. In this communication, we propose a new restoration method, which consists in choosing the Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) estimator and computing the latter thanks to a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm. We validate our method by means of realistic simulations, in two very different contexts: an astronomical observation on VLT/SPHERE and a ground-based LEO satellite observation on a 1.52m telescope. Finally, we present results on experimental images for both applications.

authors.name: Alix Yan
authors.institution: Office National d'Études et de Recherches Aérospatiales

authors.name: Laurent Mugnier
authors.institution: Office National d'Études et de Recherches Aérospatiales

authors.name: Jean-François Giovannelli
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Romain Fétick
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Cyril Petit
authors.institution: Office National d'Études et de Recherches Aérospatiales

papers.title: How Not to Be Censored: Inclusion Safety in Client-Led Consensus
papers.abstract: Blockchain consensus protocols implicitly follow a client-server architecture: validators are the only active participants, while clients (i.e., users) merely submit transactions and rely on validators to include them. This abstraction obscures a fundamental question: what should a client do to guarantee the timely inclusion of its own transaction? We study this question by introducing a leaderless consensus protocol in which clients are active. We define inclusion safety: the guarantee that a client's transaction enters some of the blocks produced for an epoch, and that every block omitting it belongs to a fork that is eventually abandoned. Because every transaction carries a reference to a block of the previous epoch, clients help select the surviving fork. This yields two paths to inclusion: reaching sufficiently many honest replicas within an epoch, or relaying a block containing the transaction across epochs until the corresponding fork becomes canonical. In a generalized model spanning synchrony and asynchrony, the client's and the replicas' connectivity are substitutes for inclusion safety: it is achieved either if the client is well connected, or if the client is poorly connected but honest replicas communicate reliably, provided the client reaches at least one of them. However, the substitution is imperfect: when inclusion safety rests on the replicas' connectivity, it requires a longer epoch compared to when the client is well connected.

papers.title: Minimax Rates for imperfect Physics-Informed Regression
papers.abstract: Physics-informed machine learning incorporates physical knowledge into data-driven models, often through a partial differential equation (PDE) that the target is assumed to satisfy. However, how much this knowledge improves statistical performance remains unclear, especially when the physical model is imperfect. Since satisfying a PDE implies being differentiable, a natural benchmark for physics-informed regression is the best achievable performance when smoothness is the only prior information about the target function. We show that there is a characteristic threshold for the modeling error above which the physical prior cannot improve the convergence rate. The form of this threshold is common to every linear PDE and certain nonlinear PDEs. Below it, the gain depends on the equation type. For classes of elliptic and hyperbolic PDEs with constant coefficients, we establish convergence rates that improve continuously as the modeling error decreases, and prove their minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors. With exact physics, the rates correspond to learning in dimension d-1 rather than d, reflecting the freedom left by unknown boundary or initial data. We also give conditions for computing the estimator with near-linear complexity and show how to tune its hyperparameters without knowing the modeling error.

authors.name: Nathan Doumèche
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: A Diagnostic Study of Faithfulness in Diffusion Language Models for Table-to-Text Generation
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models generate by iteratively denoising a masked sequence under bidirectional attention, without the strict left-to-right commitment of autoregressive decoding. Whether this difference affects how reliably they remain grounded in structured inputs is largely unexplored. We study this question in table-to-text generation using ToTTo, where highlighted source cells make factual grounding directly testable. We compare the masked diffusion models MDLM and LLaDA with GPT-2 and GPT-Neo under an identical retrieval-based few-shot protocol, together with a QLoRA-adapted LLaDA, and we score reference similarity and source grounding as separate axes. The two pull apart. Within LLaDA, additional demonstrations raise BLEU from 11.3 to 22.0 while NLI entailment against the source table falls from 0.78 to 0.52; QLoRA reaches the best BLEU of the study, 24.15, and grounds no better for it. Manual annotation shows the failure modes differ in kind: the autoregressive baselines tend to wander off the table, while LLaDA-based models more often stay on topic and swap out individual entities. Reference-based metrics alone are insufficient to assess faithfulness in table-to-text generation.

authors.name: Arthur Satouf
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Lifting PCA in the Wasserstein Space
papers.abstract: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a fundamental tool for statistical dimension reduction, yet no canonical extension to distribution-valued data has emerged within the framework of optimal transport. While Wasserstein barycenters and Wasserstein least-squares regression provide canonical liftings of Euclidean averaging and linear regression in the Wasserstein space, an analogous principle for PCA has remained unexplored. In this paper, we introduce Lifted PCA, a canonical extension of Euclidean PCA to Wasserstein space, obtained through the framework of lifting functionals in the space of probability measures by convex extension. Starting from the classical variational formulations of PCA on the Stiefel and Grassmann manifolds, we derive two equivalent minimization problems over probability measures supported on these manifolds that correspond to Wasserstein barycenters with generalized costs. We establish an exact analogue of the equivalence between the Stiefel and Grassmann formulations of Euclidean PCA, preserving PCA's original variational structure under lifting. We further derive dual formulations and optimality conditions, and establish equivalences with multimarginal optimal transport and matching-for-teams problems. We also establish statistical consistency for empirical estimators and develop computational algorithms based on the Wasserstein barycenter formulation over the Stiefel manifold. Whereas Euclidean PCA summarizes vectors through projections onto an optimal low-dimensional linear subspace, Lifted PCA summarizes probability distributions through an optimal probability measure supported on multiple low-dimensional subspaces. Numerical experiments on distributional datasets illustrate the practical performance of the proposed methodology and its benefits for distributional data analysis.

authors.name: Jérémie Bigot
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Clément Bonet
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: In vitro starch digestion kinetic, formal analysis and new kinetic model
papers.abstract: Describing mathematically the kinetics of the enzymatic hydrolysis of starch is a crucial part of nutrition and industrial applications studies. The majority of math models aim to fit the hydrolysis-extent curve ($X\_t$), so-called digestogram, whose simple shape which can be fitted equally well by various math models. A relevant model of starch digestion kinetics should be more specific of the phenomenon. This study proposes a novel analytical framework that jointly fits the hydrolysis-extent curve ($X\_t$) and the instantaneous reaction-rate coefficient ($k\_a(t)$). A large dataset comprising 672 wheat-starch time-course measurements (including normal, waxy, and high-amylose genotypes), and additional experiments on other botanical starches was analysed. Standard First-Order and Weibull models were compared with two newly derived kinetic formulations \eqref{Eq.11} and \eqref{Eq.12} based on expected starch hydrolysis' phenomenon by which $k\_a(t)$ tends with time towards an asymptotic-rate constant value, $k\_e$, following a characteristic relaxation time ($τ$). A mathematical proof of the existence of $k\_e$, specific of the type of starch, is provided, based on an analysis of the Weibull's parameters. Model ability to fit both $X\_t$ and $k\_a(t)$ was assessed by examining coefficients of determination ($R^2$) for both data types, and its adjusted version ($R^2\_{adj}$) was used to compare performances between models. All models fit very well $X\_t$ data, while $k\_a(t)$ is much more discriminant of the model formulation. Wheat starch types are well distinguished, regarding ke, by the new models, with higher susceptibility to amylase for waxy samples ($\approx 5.7\times 10^{-3} min^{-1}$), than normal ($\approx 2.2\times 10^{-3} min^{-1}$) and high-amylose ($\approx 1.7\times 10^{-3} min^{-1}$) ones. The new models outperformed the other models for monotonic evolution of $k\_a(t)$, particularly digestion of high-amylose, and allow a more accurate estimation of $k\_e$. However, the analysis also highlighted limitations for modelling non-monotonic kinetics observed for waxy wheat starch digestion, suggesting a need for more sophisticated differential-equation descriptions for $k\_a(t)$. Overall, the combined fitting strategy provides a robust method for extracting physically meaningful kinetic parameters, facilitating deeper insight into the factors controlling starch digestion and supporting the development of more accurate predictive models for glycaemic response and food processing.

authors.name: Luc Saulnier
authors.institution: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

authors.name: Jean-Philippe Ral
authors.institution: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

authors.name: Kamal Kansou
authors.institution: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

papers.title: Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity: Part I: Patterns and Posets
papers.abstract: We study permutations covered by overlapping occurrences of a consecutive pattern. Special cases of this have been studied for consecutive patterns and via the cluster method. We study enumeration sequences obtained by repeating a fixed overlap. We elicit many structural properties of such pattern covers, mainly in terms of posets whose linear extensions are in bijection with the permutations in question. The enumeration of these permutations for different patterns gives rise to a great variety of sequences, many classical, but most of them not found in the OEIS. We conjecture that, essentially, all these sequences are moments of probability measures on the real line. We develop an enumerative and order-theoretic framework for this. For overlap 1 we give a generating function whose coefficients enumerate permutations covered by any fixed pattern with any fixed number of occurrences. For overlap at most half the pattern length we derive a polynomial-time enumeration formula. We associate to each pattern, overlap, and number of occurrences a poset whose linear extensions are the corresponding permutations. The regularity of this poset construction makes possible a structural analysis that in many cases leads to enumerative formulas for large classes of patterns. We prove uniform restrictions on the local structure of the Hasse diagrams, describe their branches (pendant chains) in terms of the corresponding patterns, and characterize when the poset is a tree or chain or subdivisions of a grid. Some of these constructions yield explicit families of formulas and explain unexpected equinumerations. In a forthcoming paper we investigate the sequences arising here from a probabilistic perspective, viewing them both as point processes and as moment sequences. We also obtain integral and matrix representations for important overlap 1 and 2 classes of pattern-covering sequences.

authors.name: Mohammed Slim Kammoun
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Quenched disorder in polymerized membranes: from anomalous elasticity to a glassy phase
papers.abstract: Polymerized membranes are paradigmatic fluctuating systems in which geometry, elasticity, and statistical fluctuations combine to produce anomalous long-distance behavior. In the disorder-free flat phase, bending rigidity increases at long wavelengths while in-plane elastic moduli soften. Quenched random metric and curvature introduce competing thermal and disorder-induced fluctuations. We review perturbative and nonperturbative field-theoretical approaches to these systems, from pure membranes to their disordered counterparts. Early one-loop studies identified a disorder-free fixed point, $P_4$, and a zero-temperature disorder-dominated fixed point, $P_5$. A subsequent nonperturbative renormalization-group analysis revealed a third fixed point, $P_c$, at finite temperature and disorder, governing a continuous wrinkling transition between the thermally dominated flat phase and a disorder-dominated glassy phase. Higher-order perturbative calculations also recover a $P_c$-like fixed point, with anomalous dimensions remarkably close to the reexpanded nonperturbative predictions. This scenario connects naturally with the wrinkling transition observed in partially polymerized lipid membranes. The three experimental scaling regimes of height fluctuations can be associated with $P_4$, $P_c$, and $P_5$, with theoretical exponents showing good quantitative agreement with measurements, particularly at criticality. Finally, we discuss the status of the glassy scenario, the unresolved discrepancy between perturbative and nonperturbative fixed-point stability predictions, and possible extensions to defective graphene and related two-dimensional crystalline materials.

authors.name: D. Mouhanna
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Coherent differentiation with a monoid of degrees: derivatives, Taylor expansion, finite differences...
papers.abstract: Coherent differentiation has been introduced a few years ago as a refinement of the (categorical semantics of the) differential lambda-calculus and of differential linear logic, compatible with the determinism of computation, and hence in categories where addition of morphisms in the hom-sets is only partially defined. In this setting differentiation is implemented by a kind of ''tangent functor'', with the difference that it maps an object to its object of summable tuples rather to a tangent bundle. In our earlier work, these tuples were pairs in the case of simple differentiation, and families indexed by integers when dealing with Taylor expansion and the Fa{à} di Bruno formula. We push this idea further, considering now tuples indexed by an arbitrary commutative partial monoid satisfying a nonnegativity condition. The monoid structure on these indices plays a crucial role in the definition of the ''differential'' calculus associated with this ''tangent functor''. In that way, and without changing the general categorical infrastructure of coherent differentiation, this theory accommodates new notions of ''differentiation'' of which we describe several instances. Among many others, such notions include various forms of finite differences as well as Taylor expansion truncated at any fixed degree, and finite Taylor expansion of a fixed finite degree with a remainder.

authors.name: Thomas Ehrhard
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Aymeric Walch
authors.institution: Office National d'Études et de Recherches Aérospatiales

papers.title: The diversity of late-time interaction in Type II supernovae
papers.abstract: Studying core-collapse supernovae (SNe) beyond one year after explosion, when ejecta interaction with circumstellar material (CSM) progressively becomes the dominant power source, offers critical insights into the progenitor mass loss history. Using binary progenitors that underwent different levels of H-rich envelope stripping, we present radiative transfer calculations of the ejecta with CSM interaction in Type IIb, II-L and II-P SN scenarios covering epochs of 1.5 to 3-6yr, with a focus on the UV and optical properties. The impact of CSM interaction is evaluated for a cold-dense shell (CDS) of 0.1-2.0Msun (CDS velocity of ~5000-10000km/s) and shock powers of 1e39-1e41erg/s, producing a grid of about 200 models. We find that Lyalpha, MgII2800, and Halpha are typically the strongest individual lines, MgII2800 being the most constant relative to changes in time and in CDS mass. Lyalpha thrives at low CDS mass and is strongly attenuated otherwise. A large fraction of the emerging UV and optical flux is, however, influenced by a forest of Fe lines, which introduces strong optical depth effects. A myriad of other lines, generally forbidden, are predicted that each contain less than a percent of the total flux. N enrichment yield stronger N lines in the UV and optical. A subset of these models roughly match UV and optical observations of SNe 1993J, 1998S, 2013ej, and 2023ixf at 1.5-3yr, although matching the full range consistently is a challenge, in particular when dust must be invoked. Blue-red asymmetry of line profiles is typical of all lines in the UV, the more so at earlier times or higher CDS mass, even in the absence of dust. In our simulations, optical depth effects, associated with the gas or dust or both, quenches the emission of Lyalpha or [OIII]4958-5007A from regions within or below the CDS.

authors.name: Luc Dessart
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Mackey formulas for smooth stacks
papers.abstract: We study parabolic induction and restriction functors on derived categories of constructible sheaves, D-modules, and other sheaf theories on smooth stacks with good or adequate moduli spaces. We prove a commutation rule between them in the form of a Mackey filtration, indexed by the set of relative positions of two elements in the component lattice, a combinatorial structure that characterizes inductions and restrictions on a given stack. This generalizes similar results for adjoint quotient stacks studied in generalized Springer theory and the theory of character sheaves, and for stacks of quiver representations appearing in Lusztig's categorification of quantum groups. We also apply our result to the stack of semistable principal bundles on a curve, as a first step towards Mackey formulas in geometric Langlands correspondences.

authors.name: Lucien Hennecart
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Almost Every Pair of Interval Exchange Transformations Does Not Generate a Free Group
papers.abstract: We show that the Lebesgue measure of the set of pairs of interval exchange transformations that generate a free group of rank $2$ is zero.

authors.name: Sébastien Gouëzel
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Differential powers of monomial ideals in affine semigroup rings
papers.abstract: This article gives explicit descriptions for differential powers of monomial ideals in certain (possibly non-normal) affine semigroup rings. We use these descriptions to show that the topologies defined by the ordinary, symbolic, and differential powers of any monomial ideal are all linearly equivalent. We then prove the existence of differential signature in our settings, relating it to the volume of some convex polytope. Finally, we apply our results to pinched Veronese rings.

authors.name: Soumyadeep Misra
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Reflection functors for non-simply-laced quiver varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the braid relations between reflection functors on non-simply-laced analogues of Nakajima quiver varieties, which are defined as critical loci of certain quivers with potential. We extend this framework to categories of matrix factorizations and critical $K$-theory.

authors.name: Andrei Neguţ
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Phonon-assisted free-electron recoil control and mechanical sensing
papers.abstract: Mechanical vibrations are fundamental to a wide range of physical phenomena and technologies, yet their ability to actively shape free-electron dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we theoretically show how an optomechanical membrane provides a phonon-assisted optical interface for controlling free-electron recoil and sensing localized forces. Transverse membrane motion scatters cavity light into high-momentum evanescent sidebands that enable phase-matched interaction with electrons traveling in vacuum. Beyond supplying momentum for phase matching, the vibration amplitude controls the electron-light interaction strength and redistributes electron populations among recoil orders. External forces that perturb the vibration are thereby encoded in the electron recoil spectrum. Under the modeled conditions, electron readout of localized stochastic forces can yield a higher signal-to-noise ratio than a Gaussian optical homodyne benchmark at equal detected probe rates. These results provide a theoretical basis for mechanically reconfigurable free-electron optics and mode-selective mechanical sensing.

papers.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data via Generalized Moment Matching
papers.abstract: We study $(\varepsilon,δ)$-differentially private synthetic data for arbitrary databases of $n$ records in $[-1,1]^d$ under a specified integral probability metric (IPM). We introduce generalized moment matching, which estimates moments privately, fits a probability measure, and samples synthetic records. A general error theorem applies when moment error controls the target IPM. This framework extends Chebyshev moment matching for $1$-Wasserstein distance and smooth queries. We apply the framework to maximum mean discrepancy with Matern and Laplace kernels and a two-layer ReLU neural tangent kernel. We also obtain guarantees for sliced Wasserstein-$1$ and the IPM induced by norm-bounded ReLU networks. With sufficiently many synthetic records,these rates are minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed dimension.

authors.name: Rundong Ding
authors.institution: Key Laboratory of Automobile Materials, Ministry of Education, Jilin University

papers.title: Ergodic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Stochastic Coefficients
papers.abstract: We investigate ergodic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with stochastic coefficients and introduce the associated stochastic ergodic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, in which the classical ergodic constant is replaced by a random process $λ$. We establish well-posedness of the equation and show that $λ$ characterizes the optimal ergodic costs for a general class of averaging kernels, including those corresponding to normalized finite-horizon and discounted costs. For random-periodic coefficients, we construct a random-periodic solution and show that the optimal ergodic costs associated with all admissible averaging kernels coincide. We also establish stability of the optimal ergodic costs under perturbations of the coefficients.

authors.name: Nizar Touzi
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: VideoGen Model 1: Prompt Expansion Versus Formatting in Audiovisual Generation
papers.abstract: Creative prompt expansion improved overall audiovisual quality scores over raw prompts in a controlled pilot of VideoGen Model 1, our post-trained version of MiniMax H3. We compared the raw, reformatted, and expanded versions of 30 prompts, holding the generator, seed, and sampling settings fixed. Each clip was rated separately on five dimensions. Their mean formed an overall score on a 1-10 scale. Compared with formatting alone, overall scores increased by 0.63 points (95% interval: [+0.11, +1.15]) under VA-Judger and 0.15 points (95% interval: [-0.03, +0.35]) under Gemini 3.8 Flash, whose overall change remained uncertain. Prompt-alignment scores increased by 0.97 points under VA-Judger and 0.50 under Gemini. VA-Judger also showed higher audio quality; visual-quality ratings changed little under either judge.

authors.name: Anton Koenig
authors.institution: Office National d'Études et de Recherches Aérospatiales

papers.title: Sequential Entropic Optimal Transport for Bayesian Inverse Problems via Multilevel Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of Bayesian estimation associated to inverse problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). In most cases of practical interest, one must use numerical solvers to implement computational methods based on Monte Carlo methods. This inevitably leads to an adaptation of multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) methods to reduce computational efforts to achieve a pre-specified mean square error (MSE). MLMC is based on sampling coupled versions of Bayesian posteriors associated to increasingly precise numerical solves of the PDE. In this article we present a novel method to implement MLMC based upon sequential entropic optimal transport couplings learned with light Schrödinger bridges, and correct the transport with Metropolis--Hastings steps that preserve the pairing. We bound the mean square error associated to a version of our new estimation method and show, for an elliptic inverse problem, that to achieve a MSE of $\mathcal{O}(δ^2)$ ($δ>0$) one can have an optimal cost of $\mathcal{O}(δ^{-2})$. The results feature explicit bounds on the effect of the fitted transport and of the Metropolis--Hastings correction. From a numerical perspective, on elliptic, Darcy-flow and Navier-Stokes problems, the method reduces the variance of the most precise solver by a factor of five to ten and is faster than multilevel sequential Monte Carlo [arXiv:1503.07259] at tight accuracies.

papers.title: Learning to Reason Like a Cytopathologist:Clinically Grounded Multiscale Evidential Learning for Cervical Cytology
papers.abstract: Cervical cytology presents a fundamentally ambiguous diagnostic landscape, where equivocal categories such as Atypical Squamous Cells of Undetermined Significance (ASC-US) occupy a morphological grey zone that is definitional. For clinical decision support, the goal extends beyond assigning a definitive label to every sample: cases must also be distinguished by whether the available evidence supports a confident decision or warrants further consideration, a distinction conventional classification models are not designed to explicitly represent. We propose a multiscale evidential framework that models cervical cytology along an ordinal disease continuum using clinically grounded soft anchors, representing progression from benign reactive changes to precancerous lesions and malignancy. Three biologically motivated spatial contexts--nuclear morphology, cytoplasmic characteristics, and neighbourhood cellular architecture--are independently encoded using a shared frozen DINOv2 backbone, preserving inter-scale disagreement that early fusion may obscure. Calibrated predictions are transformed into Dempster--Shafer belief masses and fused with reliability discounting, allowing conflicting evidence and insufficient support to remain explicitly uncommitted rather than forcing a decision. The fused belief state drives interpretable routing that separates confidently classified cases from those with irreducible evidential insufficiency, enabling clinically meaningful triage. Across two independent publicly available conventional cytology datasets, RIVA and CRIC Cervix, the framework generalises consistently, with uncertainty strongly associated with diagnostic difficulty: incorrect predictions carry 1.94x-4.13x higher uncertainty than correct ones.

papers.title: PSR J0653+0443: An Eclipsing Millisecond Pulsar in an Extremely Eccentric Double Neutron Star System
papers.abstract: Double neutron star (DNS) systems emit gravitational waves (GW) as they orbit each other, with waveforms dependent on their orbital properties \cite{Poisson+2014grav.book.....P}. The number of DNS systems surviving binary star evolution in the Milky Way and the distribution of their orbital parameters are fundamental questions for GW astronomy and binary evolution studies. Here, we report the discovery of a new Galactic field DNS system, PSR J0653+0443, comprising two ~1.4 $M_\odot$ components in an extremely eccentric orbit $e=0.992387$, $P_{\rm orb}=79.084$ d. Its unique orbital dynamics include a 46-minute transit from true anomaly $θ=-90^\circ$ to $90^\circ$ and striking periastron relative motion (maximum acceleration 1.11~km~s$^{-2}$, peak speed 1.14$\times$10$^6$~m~s$^{-1}$. The pulsar undergoes an 85-second conjunction eclipse, indicating a nearly edge-on binary orbit. Short-term variations in the periastron advance induce significant pulse arrival time modulation spanning -2.91 to +2.49 ms --- at least an order of magnitude larger than that observed in any other DNS system. From this modulation, the non-relativistic periastron advance rate is constrained to $-1.5^{+0.9}_{-0.8}\times10^{-4}$ deg yr$^{-1}$. The extreme orbital eccentricity can only be attributed to a large kick velocity imparted during the iron-core collapse supernova of the progenitor of the second component. The predicted detection probability of such a PSR J0653+0443-like DNS system is $\lesssim 5 \times 10^{-3}$, implying that our discovery of this system challenges current understanding of binary evolution. This extraordinary DNS system emits periodic gravitational wave bursts, with the GW energy flux peaking at 0.357 mHz. This makes it an ideal target for the future LISAmax mission.

papers.title: On Continuous Wavelet Transform of Complex Radon Measures on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a necessary and sufficient condition for a measurable function on $\mathbb{R}^{\times} \times \mathbb{R}^{d}$ to be the continuous wavelet transform of a complex Radon measure on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ under suitable regularity conditions on the wavelets. We investigate various integrability properties of the wavelet transform of complex Radon measures. We define a new norm on the collection of such functions and show that it is isometrically isomorphic to the Banach algebra of complex Radon measures under convolution. We show a wavelet inversion formula for measures, in a restricted sense. Under additional hypothesis, we provide a reconstruction formula for the measure of closed rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^d$ using wavelet transforms. We have included supporting examples to substantiate these assumptions.

authors.name: Vaishakh Jayaprakash
authors.institution: Cochin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A KAN-based Non-linear Factorization for Embedding Layer Compression
papers.abstract: Among existing embedding compression approaches, low-rank factorization provides a simple and mathematically principled solution by approximating the embedding matrix with a reduced-rank decomposition. However, its practical effectiveness is often limited, as the resulting linear bottleneck constrains representational capacity. To overcome these limitations, we propose an enhanced factorization scheme that increases expressive power by introducing learnable non-linear projections within the compressed embedding layer. Our method is inspired by the Kolmogorov Arnold Networks (KAN) paradigm, which replaces fixed linear transformations with learnable univariate functions. Despite promising results in other domains, applications of KANs in NLP remain scarce and have so far been largely limited to final or task specific layers, rather than core representational components such as embedding layers. We evaluate the proposed approach by integrating the compressed embedding layer into the Skip-gram framework and comparing it against a standard low-rank baseline under matched parameter budgets on the Word Analogy and Semantic Similarity benchmarks. We further introduce an effective initialization strategy from a pre-trained, uncompressed embedding layer. The behavior of the model is analyzed both immediately after initialization and after a brief post-initialization refinement phase, considering training with the standard Skip-gram objective as well as variants augmented with distillation from the original embedding layer. Overall, our results show that augmenting low-rank factorization with learnable non-linear projections effectively mitigates the limitations of linear bottlenecks, yielding more faithful compressed embeddings under fixed dimensionality and suggesting a promising direction for embedding layer compression beyond purely linear methods.

papers.title: From hard-core to soft-core bosons in a shell trap
papers.abstract: We study the low-temperature states of a system of spinless bosons trapped in a broad spherical shell. In our virtual (path-integral Monte Carlo) experiments, we specifically examine how the equilibrium structure and overall superfluidity of the system are affected by a change of the interparticle-potential core from hard to increasingly soft. In this manner we bridge the gap between the behaviors of two species of bosons: Helium-like atoms, which self-assemble into ordinary crystalline solids, and Rydberg-dressed atoms, which in simulation form cluster (super)solids. We also vary the particle mass, i.e., the quantumness of the system, so as to modify the relative stability of ``solid'' and fluid states. We thus find a whole spectrum of (finite-size) phases with a curved structure, including multilayer and cluster phases, as well as superfluids and single layer supersolids. In particular, we confirm that supersolids only occur in the presence of clusters. By considering three system sizes (from 60 to 180 particles), but rescaling the trap radius so that the density stays fixed, we verify that supersolid states only exist in the same range of particle masses. Our model serves as a platform to test how emergent properties are modified, in spherical geometry, in the crossover from atoms to dressed atoms.

authors.name: F. Cinti
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia

papers.title: Logics vs doctrines, a mirror symmetry
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between doctrines, encoding 2-categories of theories in predicate logic, and fragments of geometric logic, defined through Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi. After a brief historical account of the notion of doctrine, we propose our working definition. Our main result then establishes a Galois connection between doctrines and subgeometric logics. This connection suggests a mirror symmetry between the world of doctrines and the world of logics, in which constructions and results on either side admit counterparts on the other. We develop this symmetry through constructions of syntactic categories and classifying topoi in both settings, recovering the familiar examples from categorical logic. We prove paired Diaconescu-type theorems and give symmetric universal characterisations of the two closure operators induced by the Galois connection. Finally, we show that passing from a doctrine to its closure induces a reflection between the corresponding 2-categories of algebras, and we relate this reflection to conceptual completeness.

papers.title: The role of locality and weight sharing in convolutional neural networks
papers.abstract: The success of convolutional neural networks is often attributed to locality and weight sharing. However, how these two properties separately shape learning, and how their effects depend on the spatial correlations of natural images, remain poorly understood. We address these questions in a teacher-student model with a convolutional teacher acting on $P$ input positions with correlation $c$ between positions. We compare convolutional and locally connected students trained by online stochastic gradient descent, and derive ordinary differential equations that describe their dynamics exactly in the limit of large feature dimension $D$. For uncorrelated positions ($c = 0$), the two students follow the same learning trajectory, with the convolutional student learning exactly $P$ times faster. We also find that locality affects the sample complexity: a student that matches the kernel size of the teacher recovers it from $\mathcal{O}_{D}(D)$ samples, whereas $\mathcal{O}_{D}(D\log(D))$ samples are needed with a larger kernel. For $c > 0$, spatial correlations can reduce the advantage of weight sharing. The asymptotic error of the convolutional student grows with $c$, whereas that of the locally connected student is independent of $c$ and overall lower when evaluated at the same learning rate. When the learning rate is instead tuned to the training horizon, however, the locally connected student wins at early times and the convolutional student at late times, with a transition that we predict analytically.

papers.title: Calibration scoring under dependent seed variables in Cooke's Classical Model: a Mehler-Hermite design-effect correction
papers.abstract: Cooke's Classical Model scores the statistical accuracy of experts by the $p$-value of a likelihood ratio test that compares the bin frequencies of realized seed variables with nominal probabilities, using a $χ^2$ reference. This calibration score drives performance-based weights and implicitly assumes independent seed variables, although seeds often share a common driver, such as the same indicator in several regions or periods. Under dependence the statistic converges to a weighted sum of $χ^2_1$ variables, and positive dependence makes the classical score anti-conservative. Under a Gaussian-copula working model, a Mehler-Hermite expansion gives the long-run covariance of the bin indicators in closed form, defines a design effect and an effective number of seed variables, and shows that the first-order correction coincides with the ad hoc calibration power of existing software. Rao-Scott-type and parametric-bootstrap corrected scores are proposed, together with a restricted maximum likelihood estimator of the nuisance dependence, computed from rank normal scores and invariant to location-scale miscalibration, and a prepivoted bootstrap that propagates its uncertainty. In simulations the classical score rejects up to 68\% of calibrated experts at a nominal 5\% level, whereas the corrected scores remove most of the excess rejection. In 45 published studies, design effects of 1.25-2 shift more than 5\% of the optimized weight in 29-44\% of studies. In three social-science studies with structured seeds, the baseline estimates imply that 18-21 seed variables carry the information of only 11-13 independent ones, although conclusions about individual experts depend on how the dependence is specified.

papers.title: Deflation-Based Spectral Preconditioning for the Conjugate Gradient Method on Perturbed Systems
papers.abstract: We consider sequences of large symmetric positive-definite linear systems in which spectral information from a reference matrix $A$ is reused to accelerate the solution of a nearby system with perturbed matrix $A(t)=A+tE$, where $E$ is symmetric, $\|E\|_F=1$, and $t\geq0$ is the perturbation size. We compare deflated conjugate gradient (deflated CG) with preconditioned CG (PCG) equipped with a scaled spectral preconditioner constructed from the same spectral information of $A$. First, we derive an energy-norm error characterization of deflated CG. We then use perturbation analysis to show that, after one additional PCG iteration, the squared PCG error is bounded, up to terms of order $t^2$, by an explicit multiple of the squared deflated CG error. This result clarifies the role of the scaling parameter in the preconditioner. Experiments show that the scaled spectral preconditioner recovers much of the convergence improvement provided by deflation while requiring fewer products with $A(t)$.

authors.name: Selime Gürol
authors.institution: Centre Européen de Recherche et de Formation Avancée en Calcul Scientifique

authors.name: Oussama Mouhtal
