papers.title: Cryptanalysis and Repair of "Decentralized Multi-authority ABE for NC$^1$ from BDH"
papers.abstract: We present a plaintext-recovery attack on both the DBDH-based construction and the CBDH-based variant of Datta, Komargodski, and Waters (Journal of Cryptology, 2023). The attack succeeds with probability one in the claimed static security model using one corrupt authority and two users, each unauthorized even when granted the corrupt authority's attribute. The flaw is an invalid extension of the LSSS matrix-normalization lemma originating with Rouselakis and Waters (FC,~2015): preserving complete-share distributions does not preserve coordinate-wise ciphertext masks, which a corrupt authority can expose to remove identity binding from other users' shares. For both variants, replacing these masks with independent full linear sharings of zero preserves correctness and restores ciphertext-distribution invariance. We prove static security of both repaired variants in the random oracle model under their respective BDH assumptions, using the original hardcore-bit convention for the CBDH variant. Both proofs allow adaptive identity-hash queries. The modification retains the original matrix-width and row-labeling restrictions, keys, decryption, and ciphertext size, requiring only additional encryption randomness and finite-field arithmetic. We also attack both multi-authority attribute-based inner-product functional encryption constructions of Datta and Pal (PKC, 2023) and establish correctness and matrix-substitution invariance of the same repair. We prove static security of the repaired small-universe construction under asymmetric DBDH. For the large-universe construction, we identify a missing source-group encoding in the original reduction and give a complete static security proof under an augmented $L$-DBDH assumption, whose generic bilinear group hardness we establish.

papers.title: Double-Shock Radiation in Supernova Wind Breakout and EP260321a
papers.abstract: We study the supernova (SN) shock breakout (SBO) from an optically thick stellar wind. The SN ejecta-wind interaction forms a forward shock (FS) plus reverse shock (RS) structure. The RS's internal energy and shock velocity are both a fraction $μ\lesssim1/6$ of the FS's. The lower RS velocity makes it easier to build up local thermal equilibrium (LTE) and generate blackbody (BB) emission. In the same time a $μ^{-1}\gtrsim6$ times larger non-BB emission may be produced by the likely non-LTE FS. We apply the theory to analyze the recent detected type Ic-BL SN2026gzf associated X-ray flash EP260321a, and find it is naturally accounted for by a SN wind breakout: the $\sim0.13$\,keV, thermal SBO emission can be produced by the RS during the interaction of a typical type Ic-BL SN ejecta ($E_k\sim10^{52}$erg and $M_e\sim1M_\odot$) and a stellar wind with a mass $M_w\sim10^{-4}M_\odot$ confined within a radius $r_w\sim10^{13}$cm; the X-ray rise time is mainly determined by the RS emission time, whereas the long duration and decrease time are due to the scatterings of SBO photons by a distant shell-like medium which has a large photosphere, $r_{ph}\sim10^{14}$\,cm; the early, within 30\,ks, optical emission can be naturally explained by the cooling emission of a shocked pure C/O envelope, since the observed SBO onset is delayed by $\gtrsim$ a few ks due to the large medium photosphere. BB+non-BB components from RS and FS, respectively, may be common in SN wind breakouts. SBO observations can be crucial in the study of progenitor stars by providing information for the ejecta from the SN explosion and the nearby wind from the pre-SN activities.

authors.name: Zhuo Li
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Rui-Ze Shi
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: GSP Autobidding Equilibria with Few Advertisers or Slots
papers.abstract: In sponsored-shopping auctions, one advertiser may win several positions, and a product that is never displayed may determine the prices of several winners. Under generalized second-price (GSP) pricing without self-pricing, these interactions couple allocation and payment through a single global ranking. We prove that exact autobidding equilibria under budget and return-on-investment (ROI) constraints can be computed in polynomial time whenever either the number $n$ of advertisers or the number $K$ of display slots is fixed. Our algorithms rely on two structural reductions. With few advertisers, the payment polytopes of tied bid layers combine by a Minkowski sum, giving a fixed-dimensional representation of exponentially many rankings. With few slots, budget equilibria admit threshold recovery and an exact submodular description of attainable payments at the display boundary. For ROI, we prove that every group-consecutive equilibrium has a representative with at most $K+2$ nonunit multipliers, preserving the item and price in every displayed slot. In each case, the reduction leads to polynomially many systems of polynomial equations and inequalities in bounded dimension. The algorithms compute exact multipliers and explicit distributions over valid group-consecutive rankings, with support at most $n+1$; for ROI with few slots, this improves to $\min\{n+1,K+3\}$.

authors.name: Zhengyang Liu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Lipschitz numbers and fine differentiability on metric measure spaces
papers.abstract: On a metric space equipped with a doubling measure supporting a Poincaré inequality, we introduce capacity-relaxed infinitesimal Lipschitz numbers and characterize Newtonian functions in $N^{1,p}$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and functions of bounded variation. If $X$ is additionally $Q$-regular, then every BV function is $1$-finely differentiable at $μ$-almost every point, and its fine differential agrees with its approximate Cheeger differential. We also extend a Sobolev regularity criterion from continuous to $p$-quasicontinuous functions.

authors.name: Yuxin Li
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Exploiting Pinching Antenna Systems in NOMA Covert Communication Networks
papers.abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) provide flexible transmitter-side radiation reconfiguration for high-frequency wireless communications. This paper applies PASS to non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) covert communication networks, where activated pinching antennas (PAs) transmit superimposed signals to a pair of users stochastically distributed within a rectangle. Two passive wardens respectively monitor the downlink transmissions intended for two users. More specifically, we derive the closed-form detection error probability (DEP) expressions for two wardens under bounded noise uncertainty. Then we analytically determine the optimal detection thresholds and minimum DEPs in the worst-case covert detection scenarios. The covert transmission rates of two users are further characterized by taking into consideration ideal successive interference cancellation and non-ideal successive interference cancellation at near user and intra-NOMA interference at far user. Numerical results are presented to confirm that: 1) PASS-NOMA is capable of providing higher covert rates relative to conventional orthogonal multiple access OMA schemes; 2) As the number of activated PAs begun to increase, the near user has ability to obtain a larger covert rate gain than far user; and 3) The DEP of PASS-NOMA networks is larger than that of both PASS-OMA and traditional antenna based NOMA in specific output power regions.

authors.name: Jingjing Zhao
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Xianfu Lei
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Rethinking Agentic Model Orchestration for Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) perform unevenly across forecasting tasks. Recent work uses agentic model orchestration (AMO) to select or combine TSFMs, often outperforming individual forecasters. Yet these gains may reflect stronger or more complementary candidates rather than better orchestration. To disentangle these effects, we introduce FairAMO, a controlled evaluation protocol with frozen candidate forecasts. Experiments on GIFT-Eval show that AMO improves accuracy, but its gains are bounded by the candidate TSFMs. The best orchestrators reduce MASE by less than 6% relative to the best single TSFM across all tasks. These gains depend on complementarity (different candidates excel on different tasks) rather than the number of candidates. Adding members yields diminishing returns, and a redundant member can erase these gains. The value of historical evidence also saturates quickly. A few recent windows capture all gains, and further history adds none. These findings separate system-level forecasting gains from the contribution of orchestration itself.

authors.name: Tong Guan
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology

authors.name: Tianxiang Zhan

papers.title: Sparse-grid discretizations of BGG sequences
papers.abstract: We develop the first tensor-product sparse-grid finite element discretizations of Bernstein--Gelfand--Gelfand (BGG) complexes. Alpert wavelets and their first and second primitives yield compatible hierarchies of discontinuous, continuous, and continuously differentiable piecewise polynomials, that serve as one-dimensional ingredients of BGG sparse-grid finite elements. We construct a bounded commuting sparse-grid projection that yields stable discrete potentials for Hessian, elasticity, and div-div complexes. Under mixed Sobolev regularity, we prove sparse-grid approximation estimates with dimension-independent convergence rates in the number of degrees of freedom. Experiments for a three-dimensional incompatibility problem and a two-dimensional biharmonic problem on an annulus illustrate the efficiency of sparse grids relative to full grids.

papers.title: On the Effectiveness of Snapshot Testing: An Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Software testing is essential for ensuring quality, yet testing complex front-end user interfaces is often time-consuming and difficult. Snapshot testing has emerged as a low-cost regression testing method that detects unexpected changes by comparing program behavior before and after modifications. Despite its growing adoption, empirical evidence regarding its actual effectiveness remains scarce. To fill this gap, this study presents a large-scale empirical investigation into the effectiveness of snapshot testing involving 340 GitHub repositories and a survey of 60 experienced practitioners. Our quantitative results demonstrate that combining snapshot and traditional non-snapshot tests significantly enhances code coverage, achieving a median statement coverage of 86.7%. We find that the two approaches are highly complementary, typically exercising distinct regions of the production code. Furthermore, test suites incorporating snapshot tests detected 1.3 times more mutants than those relying solely on traditional tests. Our qualitative insights from the developer survey reveal that practitioners value snapshot testing for its ease of implementation, ability to prevent regressions, and transparency in checking results. However, reviewing large result sets and managing false positives remain significant hurdles. These findings guide the strategic integration and future improvement of snapshot testing in modern development pipelines.

authors.name: Yutaro Kashiwa
authors.institution: Nara Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Bin Lin

authors.name: Hajimu Iida
authors.institution: Nara Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Higher rank spectral projector estimates and a Stein--Tomas restriction theorem
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact locally symmetric space of noncompact type. We prove sharp upper bounds for the $L^2\to L^p$ operator norms of spectral projectors for joint eigenfunctions of the full ring of invariant differential operators on $X$. This improves the corresponding result of Marshall, by removing a logarithmic power loss at the critical exponent. Using the same method, we also prove the endpoint case of Mockenhaupt's $(L^2,L^p)$ Fourier restriction theorem.

papers.title: Accelerated primal-dual dynamics and algorithms for strongly convex-concave bilinear saddle point problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop accelerated primal-dual dynamics and algorithms for strongly convex-concave saddle point problems with bilinear coupling. Combining strongly convex Nesterov dynamics with scaled heavy-ball dynamics, we propose a second-order primal-dual dynamical system with constant damping and derive an associated algorithm by time discretization and coefficient adjustment. Under suitable conditions on the continuous scaling function $β(t)$ and the discrete scaling sequence $β_k$, we establish primal-dual gap estimates of $\mathcal O(1/β(t))$ in continuous time and $\mathcal O(1/β_k)$ in discrete time. The maximal admissible growth rates of these scales recover the exponential and linear convergence rates of strongly convex Nesterov methods in continuous and discrete time, respectively. We also prove convergence of the primal-dual trajectory and sequence, even when the dual solution is nonunique. Saddle residual estimates of $\mathcal O(1/\sqrt{β(t)})$ and $\mathcal O(1/\sqrt{β_k})$ hold under globally Lipschitz gradients in continuous time and with a possibly nonsmooth dual potential in discrete time. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and the performance of the proposed methods.

authors.name: Yi-bin Xiao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Xin He
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Quantum criticality in a two-component two-dimensional nematic metal
papers.abstract: Nematic fluctuations alter the low-energy electronic behavior and reshape the mean-field phase diagram. We study a two-dimensional nematic metal with a two-component internal degree of freedom. Near the quantum critical point (QCP), longitudinal nematic fluctuations generate the non-Fermi-liquid self-energy $\propto|ω|^{2/3}$, whereas transverse fluctuations give a subleading logarithmic, marginal-Fermi-liquid correction. Nevertheless, the transverse sector dominates the correction to the phase diagram through a quantum order-by-disorder mechanism: the emergent nematic background reshapes the electronic spectrum, alters the decay of nematic bosons, and produces a negative singular free-energy correction. This correction reconstructs the phase diagram, drives the transition first order, and is described by a scaling function whose two asymptotic limits define two critical regimes with free-energy corrections scaling as $R^{8/3}$ and $R^3$, respectively, where $R$ is the order-parameter magnitude; their powers follow from the competition between the characteristic momentum of normal-state nematic fluctuations and that of the ordered-state background. These two regimes are experimentally distinguishable through nematic-susceptibility hysteresis measurements. The corrected phase diagram shows that the enlarged nodal $α$ phase masks the otherwise bare QCP, making it inaccessible; consequently, the logarithmic self-energy correction is by no means negligible at low energies.

authors.name: Yuhang Xiao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Information-Induced Conservatism Frontier of Distributed Stability Certificates
papers.abstract: Conservatism in distributed stability certification is often treated as a limitation of the certificate itself, motivating richer Lyapunov functions, tighter relaxations, or stronger optimization. But a more fundamental limitation may arise from the reporting interface: once information is compressed, physically different systems can become indistinguishable. If stable and unstable systems produce the same report, no sound method can separate them. This paper asks where this information limit lies and how much additional information is needed to move it. We model information as an information structure that partitions admissible systems into information fibers. The strongest sound certificate for a fiber is determined by its smallest stability margin, yielding a method-independent benchmark. This separates total conservatism into information-induced and method-induced parts and characterizes information order, task sufficiency, and the stability value of additional information. Three network-node studies show that network-spectrum, scalar/eigenvalue-only passivity, and independent-local reports respectively lose network--node alignment, local directional alignment, and cross-node relation. They show that critical missing information is often relational rather than dimensional. We then move from diagnosis to information design. An information-conservatism frontier gives the smallest irreducible conservatism achievable under a prescribed budget, while its inverse gives the minimum information required for a target conservatism. A witness-pair characterization turns this into a weighted covering problem. Besides, a local sensitivity law provides a computable approximation and identifies valuable unresolved quantities. The framework indicates whether conservatism should be reduced by improving the certificate or enriching the information.

papers.title: D-Pingmesh: Dynamic Probing and Fault Localization for Reconfigurable Datacenter Networks
papers.abstract: Pingmesh monitors datacenter networks through periodic pings between servers. In reconfigurable datacenter networks, topology engineering (TPE) and traffic engineering (TE) make uniform server-pair probing inefficient: a pinglist wastes budget retesting common paths while missing low-probability interfaces. Frequent control-plane updates further require rapid pinglist refresh, and cause path ambiguity at control-plane boundaries for fault localization. We present D-Pingmesh, a probing and fault-localization system co-designed with the TPE/TE control plane. Its control-plane-aware generator builds task-efficient pinglists by greedily admitting probes with high interface coverage under the current TPE/TE snapshot. An incremental replay-and-repair mechanism updates pinglists across reconfigurations rather than recomputing from scratch. At control-plane boundaries, a Rho-EM localizer jointly infers per-task old/new-path mixture weights and the fault set through EM-style iteration. We evaluate D-Pingmesh on an 8-pod reconfigurable topology under dynamic TPE/TE. At a 0.99 coverage target, D-Pingmesh uses 17.7x fewer tasks than Pingmesh and generates each pinglist about 5.1x faster than RD-Probe. In ns-3 simulation, boundary-aware localization improves micro F1 from 0.871 to 0.953 over the deTector PLL baseline. A testbed deployment demonstrates second-scale fault localization with low host overhead. These results demonstrate that D-Pingmesh is practical for reconfigurable datacenter networks with control-plane-aware monitoring.

papers.title: A Sharp Dynamic Haussler Lemma
papers.abstract: Haussler's covering lemma (JCTA 1995) gives the sharp $(C/δ)^d$ metric-entropy bound for binary VC classes under normalized $\ell_1$ distance. We prove a sharp global dynamic analogue for bounded real-valued classes in normalized $\ell_p$, for every $1\le p<\infty$. Writing $d=\operatorname{sfat}_{\varepsilon/32}(\mathcal F)$, we obtain a global dynamic cover of size at most $(C/\varepsilon^p)^d$ for every horizon and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Here a single family of deterministic causal experts, fixed independently of the instance sequence, covers every target on every sequence. For $0<\varepsilon<1/4$, a matching worst-case lower bound $(c/\varepsilon)^{pd}$ holds already for binary classes on one fixed sequence, even with real-valued experts. The constants are universal, independent of $p$. For $p=2$, this resolves the horizon-independent sequential $\ell_2$ covering problem of Rakhlin, Sridharan, and Tewari (PTRF 2015) in a stronger global form. For $p=1$, it gives the sharp $(C/δ)^{\operatorname{Ldim}(\mathcal H)}$ global dynamic covering bound for binary classes, resolving questions of Alon, Ben-Eliezer, Dagan, Moran, Naor, and Yogev (STOC 2021) and Malliaris and Moran (Trans. AMS 2024). Our proof combines rank-decreasing correction schedules and accurate sampled prefixes with exact continuations after target identification. Shared-parent routing distributes these continuations among eligible prefixes, eliminating the logarithmic overhead.

papers.title: Nonlinear Inviscid Damping of Couette Flow with Vorticity Perturbations Supported up to the Boundary
papers.abstract: We establish nonlinear inviscid damping of the near-Couette flows in a finite channel, with vorticity perturbations vanishing to infinite order at the boundary. To study the boundary effect, we decompose the vorticity into dyadic layers whose supports expand toward the boundary, and use an inductive Newton scheme to track nonlinear interactions across layers. Finally, precise elliptic estimates are established to quantify the velocity generated by different layers.

authors.name: Siming He
authors.institution: Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment

authors.name: Weiren Zhao

papers.title: On the gap of thresholds
papers.abstract: We propose an algorithm to compute the gap numbers of log canonical thresholds, anticanonical thresholds, and $\mathbb{R}$-complementary thresholds for surface pairs with a given rational hyperstandard coefficient set. As an example, we compute these gap numbers for a special hyperstandard set that appears in the effective boundedness of $n$-complements for surface pairs.

papers.title: Approximation and Inapproximability of Non-Preemptive Dial-a-Ride
papers.abstract: The non-preemptive dial-a-ride problem (DaRP) asks for a minimum-cost route of a capacitated vehicle that serves a collection of pickup-and-delivery requests, without allowing objects to be transferred or temporarily unloaded. We study this problem and the closely related minimum-ratio Steiner $k$-Forest (S$k$F) in general symmetric metrics on $n$ locations. We develop a randomized polynomial-time algorithm with expected approximation ratio $\mathcal{O}(n^{1/4}\log^{11}n)$ for the minimum-ratio S$k$F. Our algorithm combines a deterministic approximation on hierarchically well-separated trees with randomized metric embeddings. Using this algorithm, we obtain expected $\mathcal{O}(n^{1/4}\log^{12}n)$-approximations for both the non-preemptive DaRP and the S$k$F. These guarantees improve on the previous $n^{0.3+\varepsilon}$-approximation ratios for the S$k$F and the non-preemptive DaRP, where $\varepsilon>0$ is any fixed constant. Complementing these algorithmic results, we establish the first superconstant inapproximability bounds for the non-preemptive DaRP. Under the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), no deterministic polynomial-time algorithm achieves an $x^{1/(\log\log x)^c}$-approximation for some constant $c>0$, where $x$ denotes either the number of locations $n$ or the vehicle capacity $k$. Under the quantitative Gap-ETH, we rule out every deterministic polynomial-time $x^{o(1)}$-approximation. These bounds hold even on unit-edge stars with $n=(2+o(1))k$.

authors.name: Mingyu Xiao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Validating Autoformalized Specifications via Contrapuntal Languages
papers.abstract: Formal specifications can make AI-generated code mechanically checkable. Because user intent is typically expressed in natural language rather than formal logic, specifications must first be derived from it, e.g., via LLM-based autoformalization. Yet autoformalized specifications are themselves untrusted, so a key challenge is validating whether they capture user intent without relying on a costly oracle such as human review. In this oracle-free setting, a natural strategy is to vote among model outputs, but because model errors are often correlated, agreement among outputs may reflect shared mistakes rather than correctness. Our key insight is that these errors can be decorrelated through representational diversity. We achieve this diversity with contrapuntal languages: pairs of task-specific formal languages, each designed to express the intended specification, yet admitting no structure-preserving translation between them. An LLM formalizes the intent independently in each language, and we accept a specification only if a solver proves the two formalizations equivalent. To construct such languages, we present a synthesis algorithm that reuses fragments of sampled seed specifications as syntactic sugar over a base specification language. We implement the approach for first-order logic specifications and evaluate it on HumanEval+ and LiveCodeBench using GPT-5.4 mini and Qwen3.6-Flash with and without thinking. Over the strongest baseline, our method increases the proportion of accepted specifications that are correct, i.e., complete and sound, by 12.0% on HumanEval+ and 42.9% on LiveCodeBench. The accepted specifications judged complete reject 98.6% of buggy program variants on HumanEval+ and 96.2% on LiveCodeBench, compared with 92.8% and 78.3% for the strongest baseline.

authors.name: Yihan Dai
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
papers.abstract: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. We challenge this de facto design with two diagnostic findings. (1) Non-uniform computational need: items within the same sequence vary drastically in how much computation they require. Most converge after shallow processing while a critical minority only stabilizes at full depth. (2) Suboptimality of fixed allocation: given oracle access to the target item, a non-uniform depth assignment consistently outranks the fixed one, indicating that existing uniform computation both wastes capacity on already-converged items and sacrifices overall recommendation quality. These observations motivate a shift from fixed-depth computation to item-level adaptive reasoning. To this end, we propose LoopRec. LoopRec recursively applies a single weight-shared block and introduces a lightweight gate at each recursion boundary that makes a binary exit-or-continue decision for every item independently. Items whose representations have sufficiently matured exit early, while those requiring deeper reasoning continue to subsequent recursions. This design converts the fixed global depth into a learned, per-item property without auxiliary depth labels, and is readily adaptable to diverse backbone architectures. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks with four backbone families demonstrate that LoopRec consistently outperforms matched fixed-depth counterparts. Further analysis reveals that LoopRec's learned allocation exhibits interpretable patterns aligned with our post-hoc oracle analysis: lower-frequency items and more recent interactions naturally receive deeper computation. Our code is available at https://github.com/Elpmis117/LoopRec.

papers.title: Graph Topology Meets Energy-Driven Pathfinding: Preserving Contextual Consistency in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) frequently integrates knowledge graphs (KGs) for complex multi-hop question answering. However, their performance is increasingly bottlenecked by the knowledge structuring and reasoning processes. (i) Severe semantic loss: Distilling continuous texts into discrete symbols strips away contextual nuances and narrative coherence. (ii) Pronounced modality mismatch: Fragmented graph structures clash with the continuous texts LLMs are pre-trained on, while rewriting them into natural language introduces generative noise and omits information. To address these limitations, we propose ThreadRAG, a semantic-topology-based RAG framework for context-preserving knowledge structuring and modality-native evidence reasoning. ThreadRAG introduces a Semantic Topology Mapper (STM), which organizes retrieved documents into context-intact Semantic Nodes and constructs a Semantic Topology Graph (STG) through narrative, semantic, and lexical edges. It further incorporates Energy-Driven Pathfinding (EDP), which identifies query-relevant subgraphs via energy diffusion and deterministically linearizes them into coherent textual evidence paths. Experiments on three multi-hop QA benchmarks demonstrate that ThreadRAG consistently outperforms strong baselines. Notably, it achieves a 14.4% EM improvement over text-centric methods on HotpotQA and surpasses the best baseline by 5.8% EM on 2WikiMultihop, while reducing token cost to 23.3% of the strongest baseline.

papers.title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk, yet producing plausible continuations does not guarantee that they capture how scenes evolve. Under teacher forcing, strong temporal redundancy may allow local visual continuity to serve as a shortcut for current-chunk denoising, reducing the pressure to model visual evolution. We introduce Future Chunk Prediction (FCP), an auxiliary objective jointly optimized with teacher-forced denoising that predicts temporally separated chunks without access to the intervening visual context. Drawing supervision directly from training videos, FCP requires no additional pretrained visual encoder and leaves autoregressive inference unchanged. Our method achieves superior physical plausibility over standard teacher-forced autoregressive training with a lower overall training compute budget, highlighting the effectiveness and efficiency of future-chunk supervision for modeling visual evolution. Intriguingly, our visualizations suggest that FCP fosters a more structured representation space, which may be valuable for building autoregressive world models.

authors.name: Limin Wang
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University

papers.title: Charts as Epistemic Actions for Experience-Driven Agentic Data Analysis
papers.abstract: Data agents built on ReAct-style loops now execute complex analytical workflows over structured data, yet their intermediate reasoning still runs almost entirely through text. Human analysts instead move between numbers, tables, and charts, reading visual evidence to expose trends and anomalies that text summaries drop. We ask whether charts can serve as internal epistemic actions inside a data agent's reasoning loop, and how to teach an agent to use them. We first build \probe{}, a suite of 200 controlled tasks under four matched interface conditions, and find a persistent gap between what agents can read and what they choose to use. Agents score as well from self-generated charts as from numeric output, yet plotting access alone does not translate into consistent use. Task slices show that charts lead on temporal, pattern, and anomaly reasoning, while text leads on precise reading and conditional verification. We then propose \method{}, which distils two families of experience from conditioned trajectory rollouts. One family records how to select and verify analytical operations, and the other records when to invoke text, charts, or both. A trajectory judge scores outcomes and labels intermediate steps, and a validation gate admits only experience that improves held-out performance. On three held-out benchmarks with four LLM backbones, \method{} raises analytical accuracy and visual evidence quality over matched baselines, and backbones that never drew charts begin using them, all without touching model parameters.

papers.title: Measuring undergraduate students' reliance on generative AI during problem-solving: Scale development and validation
papers.abstract: Reliance on AI describes the behavioral patterns of when and how individuals depend on AI suggestions, and appropriate reliance patterns are necessary to achieve effective human-AI collaboration. Traditional measures often link reliance to decision-making outcomes, which may not be suitable for complex problem-solving tasks where outcomes are not binary (i.e., correct or incorrect) or immediately clear. Therefore, this study aims to develop a scale to measure undergraduate students' behaviors of using Generative AI during problem-solving tasks without directly linking them to specific outcomes. We conducted an exploratory factor analysis on 800 responses collected after students finished one problem-solving activity, which revealed four distinct factors: reflective use, cautious use, thoughtless use, and collaborative use. The overall scale has reached sufficient internal reliability (Cronbach's alpha = .84). Two confirmatory factor analyses (CFAs) were conducted to validate the factors using the remaining 730 responses from this activity and 1,173 responses from another problem-solving activity. CFA indices showed adequate model fit for data from both problem-solving tasks, suggesting that the scale can be applied to various human-AI problem-solving tasks. This study offers a validated scale to measure students' reliance behaviors in different human-AI problem-solving activities and provides implications for educators to responsively integrate Generative AI in higher education.

papers.title: A Multiscale Kinetic Model of DNA Damage Signalling and Repair under Combined Proton and Nanoparticle Exposure
papers.abstract: We present a multiscale kinetic framework for predicting the induction, processing, and biological consequences of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) in AG1522 human fibroblasts exposed to combined proton and 15-nm GNP irradiation. The model connects proton dose and linear energy transfer (LET), perinuclear GNP localization, secondary-electron and reactive-species production, and Poisson--Gamma-distributed lesion induction. Initial DSBs are separated into simple and complex classes and coupled to an ATM--$γ$H2AX--53BP1 signalling cascade, cell-cycle-dependent allocation among canonical non-homologous end joining, homologous recombination, alternative end joining, and single-strand annealing, and class-specific repair fidelities. The model identifies the initial complex-lesion fraction and its slower resolution, rather than post-irradiation conversion of simple DSBs, as the principal determinants of persistent damage under high-LET, GNP-enhanced irradiation. The residual-DSB results provide strong internal out-of-sample validation of the kinetic component. However, the opposing biases in correct repair and misrepair reveal an inconsistency between the class-specific fidelities and the supplied integrated-fidelity endpoint. These repair-fate predictions should therefore be regarded as model-constrained estimates pending independent measurements of correct-end joining, mutation, chromosome aberrations, and clonogenic survival.

papers.title: Core reduction for increasing neutron flux and radioisotope production in the IEA-R1 research reactor
papers.abstract: This work aims to present and analyze a new reactor core configuration for the IEA-R1 reactor core with the objective of enhancing its neutron irradiation capabilities. The reactor was modeled using the KENO-VI module from the SCALE Code System, provided by ORNL. Results have shown that implementing a near-cylindrical configuration with 20 fuel elements in the IEA-R1 core could substantially increase neutron flux, particularly in the center irradiation positions such as the EIBe (Beryllium Irradiated Element). After comparing various configurations, we conducted a brief analysis of the proposed core configuration's potential to produce 177Lu, resulting in a 34% increase in the specific activity of 177Lu considering a fuel power cycle around 21 days.

papers.title: Joint Semantic-Channel Coding and Modulation for Generative Image Transmission
papers.abstract: Digital image transmission typically optimizes source coding, channel coding, and modulation separately, limiting how source representations adapt to channel impairments. We propose SemQAM, a joint semantic-channel coding and modulation scheme for generative image transmission converting source to modulated symbols, such as standard QAM symbols. Channel impairments create two challenges: they can corrupt the latent representation at the receiver, and this corruption can compound through autoregressive coding, degrading reconstruction quality. First, SemQAM represents latent features with vector quantization (VQ), maps each VQ index to a QAM symbol, and updates the codeword corresponding to the detected symbol so that channel impairments directly affect codebook learning. Moreover, SemQAM uses the conditional expectation of received codewords to approximate the receiver reconstruction and reduce error propagation during autoregressive coding. SemQAM supports multiple SNRs and CBRs in a unified model, while also supporting conventional source coding through SemQAM-C. Experiments show that (i) under the same LDPC and QAM settings, SemQAM-C outperforms OneDC in LPIPS and DISTS with substantially lower complexity, showing that the unified model retains competitive capability for source coding. (ii) Compared with this separated counterpart, SemQAM reduces channel uses by 18.57% at matched LPIPS and outperforms the compared JSCC methods, demonstrating the benefit of joint coding.

authors.name: Zhijin Qin
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Efficient Generative Image Compression with Quantized Latents Refinement
papers.abstract: Generative image compression (GIC) delivers strong perceptual quality at low bitrates. However, GIC methods with strong perceptual quality often rely on pretrained diffusion models with high latency, while recent lightweight GIC methods reduce latency but deliver lower perceptual quality. We observe that, for lightweight GIC methods at low bitrates, coarse deterministic quantization can collapse nearby encoder latents corresponding to different fine details to the same point, making these details difficult to recover. Motivated by this, we propose GR-GIC, an efficient GIC that delivers competitive reconstruction performance with fast inference. For better performance, we introduce Guided Refinement (GR), which combines latent refinement guided by entropy context with adaptive perturbations for training regularization, jointly improving reconstruction at low bitrates. For fast inference, we introduce reorganized projected residual vector quantization (P-RVQ), which equivalently reorganizes residual updates into low-dimensional lookups to expose greater parallelism and reduce sequential computation. Experiments on Kodak show that for performance, compared with OneDC, GR-GIC achieves BD-rate savings of 23.19%, 37.71%, 22.30%, and 22.14% for LPIPS, DISTS, PSNR, and FID, respectively. For fast inference, the highly optimized implementation of GR-GIC encodes and decodes in 4.60 and 5.98 ms on an NVIDIA A100. Specifically, the reorganized P-RVQ implementation achieves a $3.14\times$ average speedup over the original implementation under the same FP32 setting. On an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, GR-GIC achieves latency comparable to lightweight GIC methods.

authors.name: Zhijin Qin
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Characterizing and Defending Utility-Hijacking in Instruction-Tuning Data Selection
papers.abstract: Instruction-data selectors choose which instruction-following records are used for fine-tuning, improving alignment quality, raising training efficiency, and filtering out harmful records. A selector's choices thus directly affect the fine-tuned model's safety, yet despite their widespread use, the security of these selectors remains under-studied. We conduct the first systematic study of adaptive supplier-side attacks against utility-oriented instruction-data selectors and introduce utility-hijacking. Utility-hijacking shapes harmful records to remain compatible with a selector while preserving their malicious payload, causing top-k selection to concentrate rather than filter the poison. Achieving both is non-trivial, because optimizing a record for score tends to wash out its payload, while bluntly preserving the payload makes the record look low-value. Our generate-and-rerank procedure generates, per instruction, many payload-bearing candidates and submits only the highest-scoring survivor. Evaluated across three payloads (over-refusal, false-fact injection, and insecure code), six selectors, and victim models from Qwen2.5-7B to Qwen3-32B, utility-hijacking drives refusal from 0% to 94% and insecure code up to 56/90, while false-fact enrichment intensifies with scoring-model scale from 2.84x to 7.04x. To defend against this attack, we propose CONCERT, a targeted defense needing no content detector or poison labels. It flags suppliers selected far more often than chance allows, then re-selects under the same budget, keeping only records that two dissimilar selectors both rank highly. On a Qwen3-32B victim, CONCERT reverses the poison concentration from 6.67x to 0x (code) and 3.59x to 0.67x (facts), and reduces downstream harm by 100% and 75% respectively, at unchanged capability.

authors.name: Yahao Ren
authors.institution: Shanghai University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: When Do Gaussian Priors Fail? A Latent Geometry Investigation of RL Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Latent diffusion models almost universally place a Gaussian prior on the VAE latent space. For base generation this default is unproblematic; under reinforcement-learning fine-tuning, however, it carries a structural limitation. The standard VAE's KL term does not merely ignore mode structure - it actively taxes separation and tightness. When data are multimodal, the ELBO optimum compresses distinct modes into an overlapping latent. RL fine-tuning amplifies this overlap: the score network is under-resolved on the saddle region between modes, dynamic-to-variational amplification rises sharply, and the collapse boundary beta_c is pushed far above its variational scale. On the real alanine-dipeptide Boltzmann distribution, a Gaussian-prior VAE collapses at beta_c = 0.224 while a mode-tracked Gaussian-mixture prior collapses at 0.00316, a 71x gap from the same pipeline. We trace this gap to a single geometric mediator, d_min/(2 sigma_0), and verify the causal chain through controlled interventions: moving geometry at fixed prior, and switching prior at matched geometry (full mediation; prior-label coefficient 0.995x, 95% CI [0.79, 1.25]). A three-source decomposition localises the amplification to the learned policy (zero ODE-solver contribution, bounded anchor mismatch); the coverage plateau is an unconditional benefit of mode-separating priors that no amount of RL capacity recovers. The remedy is conditional: a non-Gaussian prior is necessary precisely when the latent geometry would fall into overlap and the task is coverage-sensitive. A machine-checked theory skeleton supports the KL pricing structure - a divergent compactness tax under a Gaussian prior versus a finite assignment fee under a mixture - and the position-versus-plateau distinction delimits what is finite-resource from what requires changing the prior.

authors.name: Wang Ru
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: Implicit Feature Reweighting for Label-Free Graph Generalization
papers.abstract: Graph-level out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization is critical for deploying graph neural networks in real-world applications where distribution shifts are inevitable. Existing approaches typically require class labels during representation learning to decide which substructures are predictive, limiting their applicability. We propose SCARCE, a label-free representation-learning framework that yields distribution-shift-robust graph representations from an environment partition of the training graphs alone, whether that partition comes from dataset metadata or, when none is available, from clustering a self-supervised embedding. Our method operates in two stages: (1) a variational graph autoencoder is warm-started for graph reconstruction; and (2) an adversarial confusion mechanism forces the encoder to produce representations from which a discriminator cannot distinguish environments, while preserving graph-reconstruction fidelity. We provide theoretical analysis showing that environment confusion contracts environment-discriminative directions in the representation space, which, under regularized downstream classifiers, is equivalent to imposing a stronger directional penalty on environment-associated features. This feature-reweighting mechanism reduces reliance on spurious correlations without erasing information, offering a label-free, continuous relaxation of last-layer reweighting methods. Experiments on a controlled synthetic datasets and the DrugOOD datasets show that SCARCE achieves state-of-the-art OOD generalization among label-free methods, using no class labels during representation learning.

authors.name: Tianjun Yao
authors.institution: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

authors.name: Xinyang Li
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: Lineage-Aware Search Control for LLM-Based Evolutionary Factor Mining
papers.abstract: Formulaic alpha factor mining searches for symbolic expressions that transform market data into predictive signals. Recent LLM-based evolutionary factor mining methods use large language models as semantic variation operators. Under the conventional LLM-EA paradigm, stochastic variation and fitness-based selection can leave the search weakly directed and concentrated around a narrow set of structurally similar factors. We argue that these limitations arise because current methods mainly organize search at the individual and population levels, leaving lineage-level control underused. A lineage connects successive factor variants through evolutionary descent. We propose LineageEvo, which uses lineage in two coupled forms of search control: (1) lineage-conditioned LLM variation, which distills Lineage-Scoped Search Experience into operator-specific priors and fuses them with global operator priors, providing persistent, lineage-relevant guidance for LLM generation; and (2) lineage-stratified search allocation, which balances factor quality against lineage concentration by distributing the search budget across lineages during evolutionary search. Together, these mechanisms make semantic variation more direction aware and prevent branches from dominating the evolution, thereby promoting the discovery of predictive and diverse factors. We evaluate LineageEvo on CSI 500 and S&P 500 in terms of factor predictiveness, portfolio performance, search efficiency, and lineage- and expression-level diversity. LineageEvo achieves the strongest predictive performance on both markets, while LSPS produces a more balanced lineage distribution and a structurally broader factor pool. The results support lineage as a useful intermediate unit for controlling LLM-based evolutionary factor search.

papers.title: Some Results on the Weight Spectrum of Binary Reed-Muller Codes $RM(m-7,m)$
papers.abstract: We study the set of weights occurring in the high-order binary Reed-Muller codes $RM(m-7,m)$. For every $m\geq 14$, we prove that the weight spectrum contains all even weights in $[336,2^m-336]$, together with an explicit finite set of low weights and their complements. The proof first establishes the corresponding base-code inclusion in $RM(7,14)$. This base step uses four-block concatenation, explicit degree-six monomial witnesses, and known spectrum inputs for $RM(5,10)$ and $RM(6,12)$. The base inclusion is then lifted to all $m\geq 14$ by a concatenation-based induction. We also analyze the remaining base-code target weights $322,326,330,334$ in several restricted families, including four-block branches, affine-flat and structured inner corrections in a fixed Carlet-type Maiorana-McFarland outer shell, and sparse sums of degree-7 coordinate monomials. The residual analysis delineates several construction routes that cannot yield the four unresolved base-code weights, thereby sharpening the remaining $c=7$ spectrum problem.

authors.name: Bo Zhou
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

papers.title: LLM-Based Exogenous World Modeling for Dynamic Scheduling
papers.abstract: Dynamic scheduling requires dispatching online arrivals while anticipating future jobs, as poor decisions can compound downstream costs under nonlinear tardiness objectives. We show that a pretrained large language model (LLM) can serve as the exogenous component of a structured world model, forecasting uncertain future job arrivals. Specifically, we exploit an afterstate decomposition, which separates known deterministic shop transitions from uncertain exogenous job arrivals, enabling the LLM to forecast only the latter through a compact belief representation. Building on this, we develop Afterstate World-Model Planning (AWMP), which combines an evolved, belief-conditioned dispatching strategy with short scenario-based rollouts. A surprise-triggered refresh mechanism queries the LLM only when newly observed arrivals deviate sufficiently from previous forecast, and online residual self-calibration further conditions the LLM on its recent forecast errors to handle nonstationary arrivals. Across diverse arrival distributions, AWMP reduces weighted tardiness by 6-21% on dynamic job-shop and 22-46% on flexible job-shop benchmarks, relative to the best of eight classical priority-dispatching rules.

authors.name: Jianan Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Seeing through Denoising: Frequency-guided One-step Denoising for Infrared Small Target Detection
papers.abstract: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) is a challenging task due to the extremely small size of targets, low signal-to-noise ratios, and heavy background clutter in infrared imagery. While the progress of deep learning has advanced this field, existing methods primarily adopt discriminative paradigms that directly map images to target masks, overlooking the potential of generative modeling. In this paper, we propose DiffIRSTD, a novel generative framework that reformulates infrared small target detection as a background reconstruction problem. Instead of explicitly predicting target regions, we reinterpret small targets as noise-like signals and leverage a diffusion-based model to recover a clean, target-free background from a perturbed input image. The residual between the reconstructed background and the original image is then exploited to highlight candidate target regions, providing explicit cues for subsequent detection. To address the computational cost typically associated with diffusion sampling, we introduce a one-step denoising strategy that enables efficient background reconstruction while maintaining practical inference speed. Furthermore, we present a frequency-guided perception loss to preserve high-frequency background details and focus more on the reconstruction quality of target regions. More importantly, our DiffIRSTD operates as a plug-and-play framework, compatible with existing IRSTD models without increasing the computational complexity of detectors. Extensive experiments on IRSTD-1K, NUAA-SIRST, and NUDT-SIRST datasets demonstrate the superiority of our method, achieving state-of-the-art performance across three benchmarks.

papers.title: Nominate-then-Adjudicate: LLM-Assisted One-Pass and Per-Instance MIP Solver Tuning
papers.abstract: Mixed-integer programming solvers expose hundreds or even thousands of parameters whose best setting varies per instance, yet per-instance search is prohibitively expensive. We frame this as configuration for heterogeneous Big Data optimization workloads and propose a nominate-then-adjudicate pipeline built around two design choices. First, a fixed portfolio is sampled once and reused across instances, removing per-instance configuration search at inference; on the evaluated families, the resulting shortlist retains substantial oracle headroom, making selection within it the empirical focus. Second, the fixed 20-feature representation can map structurally different instances to the same vector, preventing a feature-only selector from distinguishing them even when they prefer different configurations. The foundation model receives no task-specific weight updates, and selection is one-pass: one model call and no solver calls at inference. The study represents structural Variety through distinct formulation families and decision Value through solver-performance outcomes; the one-call, zero-solve protocol specifies the decision interface and leaves end-to-end latency unmeasured. Among comparisons exceeding a 20% practical-difference threshold, the complete adjudicator records 538 wins and 185 losses against the top nominee, while its win rate against the default rises from 84.9% to 90.2%. Against per-instance configuration baselines under a matched one-pass protocol it leads the cluster-level methods and the best-performing evaluated per-instance baseline, ISAC+.

authors.name: Yifan Zhao
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xinyu Guan
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Frobenius forms and semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras
papers.abstract: We determine the Nakayama automorphism of the canonical homogeneous Frobenius form on cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras. We give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions on the dominant weight and the rank for semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras of types $A_e^{(1)}$, $C_e^{(1)}$, $A_{2e}^{(2)}$, $D_{e+1}^{(2)}$, $A_\infty$, $B_\infty$, and $C_\infty$. As an application, we prove that a cyclotomic Hecke--Clifford superalgebra is semisimple if and only if the corresponding Poincaré polynomial is nonzero.

authors.name: Shuo Li
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: A high-order multi-scale method and its error analysis for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems in composite materials
papers.abstract: Significant spatial heterogeneity and nonlocal history-dependent attenuation jointly govern wave propagation in composite materials, making full-scale direct numerical simulation (DNS) computationally prohibitive. This study proposed a high-order multi-scale (HOMS) method for nonlocal-in-time fractionally damped wave problems with highly oscillatory and discontinuous material coefficients. Using a multi-scale asymptotic expansion approach, the macroscopic homogenized equation, and first- and second-order correction terms are derived to construct the high-accuracy HOMS solution. Moreover, a local pointwise error analysis identifies the leading residual eliminated by this HOMS solution and validates its local physical balance preservation. Then, a global energy-norm error estimate establishes the $O(\varepsilon)$-order convergence rate for the HOMS solution. Subsequently, an efficient spatiotemporal multi-scale algorithm integrating the finite element and finite difference methods is designed, which employs a novel fully discrete $L2\text{-}1_σ$-Newmark scheme, and corresponding unconditional shifted-energy stability and explicit convergence rates are also obtained for the macroscopic homogenized displacement and velocity, respectively. Both two- and three-dimensional examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy, efficiency, reduced cost, and robustness of the proposed HOMS method. This work provides an effective multi-scale tool for nonlocal-in-time wave simulation in engineering applications.

papers.title: RegoMender: A Multi-agent Framework for Automated Rego Policy Repair
papers.abstract: Policy-as-Code (PaC) has emerged as a foundational paradigm in cloud-native systems. However, repairing Rego policies remains challenging due to their strict syntax, declarative semantics, and specific verification requirements. Existing automated program repair (APR) methods are mainly designed for mainstream languages and struggle to accommodate the unique policy logic and repair workflows of Rego. Thus, Rego policy repair remains a manual process driven by trial and error. To address this, we introduce RegoBench, the first automated Rego policy benchmark comprising 1,159 real-world defects, and propose RegoMender, a feedback-guided multi-agent framework. Collaborating via a shared blackboard and an atomic toolkit, RegoMender dynamically executes patching, rewriting, or rolling back, to resolve complex repair scenarios. Evaluated on RegoBench, RegoMender achieves syntactic and test-based semantic success rates of 82.9\% and 77.9\%, respectively, outperforming the strongest baseline by 13.4\%. Unlike other approaches whose performance drops in complex scenarios, RegoMender maintains effectiveness across single-step and chained repair tasks. Furthermore, it generalizes strongly across HCL and SQL and achieves an 86.4\% repair rate on 132 real-world CVE vulnerabilities, proving its robustness and practical utility for security.

authors.name: Li Hu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Fanqi Kong
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University

authors.name: Shaoyin Cheng
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Property (R) with its stability for analytic functional system and under compact perturbations
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}_T$ be the analytic functional system generated by a linear bounded operator $T$ on an infinite dimensional complex Hilbert space. This paper characterizes the stability of property (R), a variant of Weyl's theorem, for $\mathcal{F}_T$ and under compact perturbations in terms of the spectrum on consistency in Weyl. In particular, the stability of property (R) under compact perturbations is shown to imply the (R)-stability of $\mathcal{F}_T$.

papers.title: Geospatial Dynamics of Online Attention to Nuclear Power in Japan Before and After Fukushima
papers.abstract: Nuclear power is increasingly seen as necessary for sustainable development, but this role depends on informed public engagement and support. Building this support requires understanding what citizens want to know, as reflected in their spontaneous online searches. To map this demand, we present the first long-term (2004-2024), prefecture-level analysis of Google Trends data on nuclear power in Japan. The results indicate that in routine periods, search interest followed a host-locality pattern, being significantly higher in prefectures hosting nuclear plants, with little spillover to their neighbors. Immediately after the Fukushima Daiichi accident in March 2011, this pattern changed, and interest instead declined with distance from Fukushima, before the host-locality pattern returned from 2012. During March 2011, searches leaned heavily toward general and live information rather than guidance on what to do. Their framing also varied with proximity, as those near Fukushima prioritized live updates and formal countermeasures, while others leaned toward background information and personal-scale questions. These patterns and the shift between them provide a behavioral evidence base for designing communication strategies in Japan and countries weighing the use of nuclear power. More broadly, the finding that searches vary with proximity can inform public communication in other geographically anchored crises.

authors.name: Yifan Sun
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: CORD: Conflict-Aware Optimization for Joint RL and Distillation in Agents
papers.abstract: Joint reinforcement learning and self-distillation combines task rewards with dense teacher guidance for agent training, but their gradients can partly cancel. A mixing coefficient controls relative scale without selectively removing opposing components. We present CORD, a general framework for conflict-aware optimization of two objectives. CORD separates the choice of protected objective from the condition that triggers projection, and combines the gradients once per optimizer mini-batch. A nearest-point formulation yields a closed-form update and characterizes its first-order effect on the protected objective before optimizer transformations. Gradient diagnostics connect conflict in agent training to lost local optimization progress and motivate selective correction. As a gradient-combination mechanism, CORD can be added to different joint training recipes while retaining their objectives. Across three such recipes, it improves ALFWorld success by 1.5-15.9 percentage points. On WebShop, it improves two of the three pairs, with SDAR rising from 60.7% to 64.6% success. Our analyses explain why protection direction and projection gate must be chosen together, and why the distillation objective and its mixing weight remain consequential after projection.

authors.name: Wenhao Yu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Junyan Lyu
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Attn-Forcing: Learning Full-Context Attention Proxies for Streaming Video Generation
papers.abstract: Increasing the attention context length significantly improves streaming video generation quality, while incurring prohibitive memory and computational costs as the context grows. Existing methods attempt to capture this contextual information through attention selection or compression, but remain limited by bounded representations and lack explicit attention-level supervision to retain historical contributions to current queries. To address this, we introduce Attn-Forcing, a novel framework that preserves full-context attention contributions for streaming video generation under bounded memory and computation. We achieve this by introducing attention proxies that continuously approximate the attention responses induced by the historical context. Specifically, we implement the proxies as learnable visual latents and employ a Proxy Update Module to incorporate visual context from historical latents. Moreover, we propose an Attention Matching Loss to explicitly constrain the attention behavior of the learned proxies using full-context attention supervision. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate that Attn-Forcing consistently improves streaming video generation quality and achieves state-of-the-art performance over existing baseline methods.

authors.name: Yanan Sun
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Hanxin Zhu
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: PEEK: One-Step-Look-Ahead Exposure Bias Correction for Diffusion Sampling
papers.abstract: Diffusion image generators are successful due to accurate denoising networks and strong numerical samplers. Yet the two components are not fully matched. During sampling, the denoiser predicts for the next step based on flawed input that differ much from the real data. This train-test gap, or exposure bias, caps image generation quality (i.e., blurry, lacking in details or awkward in shape). To mitigate the problem, we propose PEEK, a novel training-free deterministic sampler plugin. At each eligible denoising step, PEEK first performs a provisional one-step update, evaluates the denoiser once at the look-ahead state, and interpolates it with the one-step-later prediction to form the next noisy state. By taking the additional step, we obtain a generally more-image-like prediction from the higher-signal noisy state, mitigating the exposure bias. To optimize the interpolation positions, PEEK searches for an interpolation schedule search made efficient by the prefix and baseline noise-schedule-rebasing caches. On 8 pixel-space and latent-space diffusion models with unconditional, label-guided, and text-guided settings across various output resolutions, PEEK consistently improves over NFE-matched baselines, with FID improvements up to 49.3\% at minimal extra computation cost (e.g., the one-time-per-model calibration takes at most 2.2 minutes across our experiments.). Project website is at https://dachengruoque.github.io/PEEK-Video/.

authors.name: Yunwei Bai
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Ying Kiat Tan
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Intertwined complex orbital order and ferrimagnetism in honeycomb molybdate Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent experimental interest in honeycomb molybdates A$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, we return and develop the minimal models to capture the essential physics for Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$. It is pointed out that, the magnetism in these materials arises from the mutual induction between the spin-orbit coupling of the tetrahedral sublattice with active orbitals and the superexchange with the spins from the octahedral sublattice. Essentially, the superexchange between the tetrahedral and octahedral sublattices directly drives the ferrimagnetism, and the residual spin-orbit coupling on the tetrahedral sublattice induces the complex orbital order. The hybrid magnon-phonon excitations are further explored together with their resulting Berry curvatures and thermal Hall effect. We discuss the experimental relevance with Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, and the framework can be extended to FeNiMo$_3$O$_8$, Ni$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$ and other isostructural magnets.

authors.name: Gang v. Chen
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Quantum Matter

papers.title: DGCM-SSFA: Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulation and Sparse Strip Frequency Attention for Efficient 3T-to-7T MRI Synthesis
papers.abstract: Synthesizing high-fidelity 7T MRI from routinely acquired 3T scans offers a practical pathway to enhanced neuroimaging without the prohibitive cost of ultra-high-field scanners. While existing deep learning approaches have achieved promising results, state-of-the-art methods typically rely on either large-scale architectures exceeding 45 million parameters or computationally intensive ensemble strategies, limiting their practicality in resource-constrained clinical environments. In this work, we propose a compact multi-domain attention framework, termed DGCM-SSFA, that achieves competitive synthesis quality with only 11M parameters. The proposed architecture integrates two complementary modules into a U-Net Transformer backbone. First, a Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulated Feature Modulator (DGCM) is embedded at multiple hierarchical levels to enhance local edge and texture details through Sobel-guided spatial attention and depthwise frequency-aware channel attention with cross-branch gating. Second, a Sparse Strip Frequency Attention (SSFA) module at the bottleneck captures global spatial context via strip-pooled attention with near-linear complexity, while simultaneously performing FFT-based spectral modulation in the frequency domain. These two modules operate synergistically with the backbone's native channel attention, forming a triple-granularity feature refinement pipeline. Extensive experiments on the UNC and BNU 3T-to-7T MRI datasets across T1w and T2w modalities demonstrate that DGCM-SSFA achieves strong structural fidelity, attaining an SSIM of 0.8431 on BNU T2w---approaching the best benchmark value of 0.8624---and 0.8100 on BNU T1w, while using substantially fewer parameters than Transformer-based alternatives such as ResViT (123.4M) and FS-RWKV (45.4M).

authors.name: Zhonghua Xie
authors.institution: Heilongjiang University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Benchmarking and Error Analysis of Deep Search and Deep Research LLM Agents
papers.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) evolve into autonomous Deep Search and Deep Research Agents capable of executing long-horizon, multi-step tasks, evaluating their reliability becomes increasingly critical. However, existing evaluation paradigms predominantly focus on final task outcomes, leaving a significant gap in understanding the intermediate execution traces, where agents are highly susceptible to various errors. To address this critical gap, we introduce a comprehensive methodology and analytical framework designed specifically to diagnose errors in intermediate workflows. Building upon this framework, we establish a structured taxonomy that categorizes these vulnerabilities into two primary dimensions: System-Level Errors and Task-Level Errors. Through a systematic examination of step-by-step execution traces and agent-environment interactions, we reveal how these underlying errors affect overall performance. Finally, through empirical experiments and systematic analysis of the identified error types, we provide actionable design guidelines, aiming to enhance the robustness, reasoning capabilities, and reliability of Deep Search and Deep Research agents.

authors.name: Zhenheng Tang
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xiaowen Chu
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Dynamical Tunneling Blockade in Layer-Pseudospin Ferromagnets
papers.abstract: Double-layer systems with narrow or flat electronic bands may exhibit spontaneous interlayer coherence, described by a layer-pseudospin ferromagnetic order parameter. In modern realizations of layer-pseudospin ferromagnets, the electrons carry additional valley degeneracies, endowing each layer with a valley-pseudospin degree of freedom. We study their nonequilibrium steady states driven by a static interlayer voltage bias in the presence of interlayer tunneling. While in the low-bias regime, the system is in a static state with parallel valley pseudospins between the two layers, we show that in the high-bias regime, the dynamical precession of the layer-pseudospin stabilizes the valley pseudospins in the antiparallel configuration, strongly suppressing the interlayer tunneling. This dynamical tunneling blockade leads to an absence of ac current and a sharp drop of the dc tunneling current to a tiny value, in stark contrast to conventional quantum Hall double layers.

authors.name: Yuta Murakami
authors.institution: Institute for Materials Research, Tohoku University

papers.title: A quaternary Diophantine inequality with prime numbers of a special form (II)
papers.abstract: Let $N$ be a sufficiently large real number. In this paper, it is proved that, for $1<c<\frac{5179}{3909}$ and for any arbitrary large number $E>0$, the Diophantine inequality \begin{equation*} \big|p_1^c+p_2^c+p_3^c+p_4^c-N\big|<(\log N)^{-E} \end{equation*} is solvable in prime variables $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4$ such that each of the numbers $p_i+2\,(i=1,2,3,4)$ has, counted according to multiplicity, at most $[\frac{31250}{5179-3909c}]$ prime factors, which constitutes a large improvement upon the previous results of Dimitrov [13] and Li-Xue-Zhang [22], respectively.

authors.name: Yuhua Zhao
authors.institution: Hebei Normal University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Linji Long
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology - Beijing

papers.title: Fig: Automated Multiagent Behavior Elicitor
papers.abstract: Many social evaluations for multiagent systems study behaviors as they emerge from environments instead of systematically intervening in the environment to elicit such behaviors. We introduce Fig (Finding Interactions in Games), an agentic system that performs targeted elicitation interventions on game environments. It takes a natural language behavior description, decomposes it into sub-behaviors, generates new social games or selects existing ones, and executes single or combined interventions to the games' engine, opponents, instructions, and context. To evaluate model behavior, it combines built-in mechanical checks and synthetic rubric judgments. We validate the interventions, generated games, and evaluation mechanisms via human review. Models attempt the target behavior in 45.2% of episodes on average for valid scenarios generated by Fig for six test behaviors -- cooperation, exploitation, deception, covert coordination, betrayal, and sabotage. For game-behavior pairs with available controls, Fig's interventions increase attempt rates by 10.9% on average compared to matched control games. Fig shows that multiagent environments can serve as programmable test beds for intentional, controllable, and reproducible behavior evaluation. Code is available at https://github.com/fleet-ai/fig.

papers.title: AgentPolicyForge: From Executable Environments to Policy Benchmarks and Adaptive Guards
papers.abstract: Customized agent deployments define policies over tools, resources, and execution conditions. Providing these policies in the task agent's prompt does not reliably prevent violations. Training a guard requires examples of tool calls that comply with or violate those policies. We introduce AgentPolicyForge, a framework that uses executable environments to construct policy benchmarks and iteratively train policy guards. With this framework, we construct PolicyGym, a dataset across ten policy families using 698 scenarios for training data generation and 254 separate held-out scenarios for human-reviewed test sets. Tool calls are executed and their outcomes recorded to help determine whether they comply with the policy. Every violating case uses a permitted tool, requiring checks of arguments, resources, and context rather than tool identity alone. The case construction process supports iterative guard training: an attacker generates requests using retrieved strategies, and the guard is fine-tuned on balanced, environment-verified examples. Training improves policy enforcement even with a fixed archive. Updating the archive further reduces in-domain attack success compared with keeping it fixed. We compare policy-aware task agent self-regulation with a trained policy guard. On PolicyGym, the final guard-based configuration achieves a 40-44% relative reduction in attack success rate and fewer benign rejections than policy prompting alone.

authors.name: Chao Shang
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: Rethinking Time Series Tokenization from a Frequency Perspective
papers.abstract: Tokenization that partitions time series into subsequences has become a foundational paradigm in modern time series modeling. However, we find that current tokenization strategies inherently introduce spectral distortions, forcing the learned representations to diverge from the true underlying patterns such as trend, periodicity, and seasonality, thereby impairing model performance. Through theoretical analysis from a frequency perspective, we derive the boundary conditions under which such distortions occur. To overcome this distortion, we propose TimeFT, a nearly distortion-free frequency-based tokenizer for time series data. TimeFT obtains tokens through frequency-domain partitioning, frequency shifting, and Nyquist sampling. The method is parameter-free, incurs negligible computational complexity, and can serve as a drop-in replacement for existing tokenizers. Our extensive experiments on diverse tasks such as forecasting, classification, and anomaly detection demonstrate that TimeFT consistently and significantly improves performance.

papers.title: Influence of embedding depth on the pullout of a plate from a confined granular medium
papers.abstract: Understanding the behaviour of moving objects within confined granular media is important in many technical applications. In this work we study the vertical pullout of a plate-like intruder buried at different depths within a dense granular aggregate from the onset of motion to flow around the intruder in the steady state by means of a two-dimensional polygonal Discrete Element Method. We find that the peak and steady-state drag forces depend differently on their embedding depth for different friction coefficients. Depending on the strength of friction the plate may interact with the domain walls, which enhances the drag force until failure of the aggregate, but not in the steady-state as dilation around intruder directs the force chains emanating from the plate upwards and away from the walls. If the inter-particle friction is weak, it is possible for the overhead pressure to overcome frictional resistance beyond a certain embedding depth. This prevents the formation of dilated failure zones above the intruder and changes the failure mode of the aggregate, leading to a slower decay of the steady-state drag forces with pullout distance.

authors.name: Shun Nomura
authors.institution: Tokyo University of Marine Science and Technology

papers.title: Non-trivial intersecting families for direct products
papers.abstract: A family of sets is intersecting if any two of its sets intersect, and non-trivial intersecting if there is not any element which appears in every set of the family. The study of intersection problems (or Erdős-Ko-Rado problems) on families of sets is one of the most important topics in extremal combinatorics. A natural extension of the Erdős-Ko-Rado problem in direct products setting was introduced by Frankl, and developed by Alon and Katona et al. In 2018, Kwan, Sudakov and Vieira [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. A 156 (2018), 44--60] determine the maximum size of a non-trivial intersecting direct product family under the assumption that the sizes of all parts are sufficiently large relative to the set sizes in all parts. Meanwhile, they raised the question of whether this result holds for the size of each part which depends only on its corresponding set size, and the question of characterizing the extremal families. In the present paper, we answere these two questions. Furthermore, the bounds on the size of each part in our result are best possible.1

authors.name: Jian Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Our Own Jev: Typed Decisions in One Forward Pass, from an In-House Judge to Open LoRA Models
papers.abstract: A typed decision maps evidence, a question and a fixed set of options to a probability for every option, computed in one forward pass, by reading a language model's logits or a small head over its hidden states, instead of generating and parsing text. The commercial system Jev popularised this System~1 interface, and open reproductions have followed. We report two uses of the pattern. \emph{Part I} describes an in-house System~1 judge that triages about 148K agentic coding session records for a training corpus.
